Climate change affects every aspect of life, and everyone has a responsibility to do their part in mitigating its impact. In this regard, the HKMA has devoted substantial efforts to driving Hong Kong's climate goals and contributing to the enhancement of global climate resilience and sustainable development. Following the inclusion of our inaugural sustainability report as a chapter in the HKMA Annual Report 2021 last year, we are publishing the Sustainability Report 2022 as a standalone publication for the first time this year. I hope this report will provide readers with a deeper understanding of the HKMA's strategies and priorities in strengthening the climate resilience of Hong Kong's banking system, building a green finance ecosystem, and fulfilling our roles as a responsible investor and a sustainable organisation. During the year, we made significant progress in advancing sustainability across the HKMA's major functions. You will learn about our specific measures and initiatives in this report, with the following key highlights: Banks face climate risks in their daily operations. As the banking regulator, the HKMA has taken concrete measures to strengthen banks' climate resilience. In 2022, we formulated a two-year plan to integrate climate risk factors into our supervisory processes and explored how to harness the power of technology to assist banks in assessing the impact of physical risks. Seeing the increasing number of green and sustainable products launched by banks, we also shared good practices with the industry on how to properly manage these products, with a view to promoting banks' capacity in climate risk management. The HKMA actively participates in various collaborative initiatives related to addressing climate risks and promoting sustainable finance development. Locally, we are working with other financial regulators through the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group) to develop a local green classification framework; the framework will enhance transparency in the financial markets and align green finance policies more closely. At the international level, we are actively participating in various international organisations to assist in formulating climate change policies and assessing their impact on financial stability. Hong Kong is well-positioned to meet the demand for green and sustainable financing in the Asian region. Although 2022 was a rather difficult year for the global bond market, green and sustainable debt issuance in Hong Kong continued to record strong growth, increasing by 42% to reach a total issuance size of US$80.5 billion, making it the largest centre for arranging international green and sustainable bond issuance in Asia². Relevant issuers included the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government and the Hainan Provincial People's Government, whose issuances once again demonstrated Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating green and sustainable capital flows between the Mainland and the international market. The flourishing development of Hong Kong's green bond market is also partly attributable to the Government Green Bond Programme. Since 2019, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds totalling nearly US$16 billion, with the raised funds allocated to over 40 green government projects, including green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency and energy conservation. We also assisted the Government in achieving "firsts" in two aspects, including assisting the Government in issuing the inaugural batch of retail green bonds worth HK$20 billion in May 2022, which was the largest green retail bond issuance globally at the time. In addition, we assisted the Government in issuing the inaugural tokenised green bond in February 2023. This is the first tokenised green bond issued by a government globally, and the issuance also marks a milestone in our successful integration of strengths in the bond market, green and sustainable finance, and fintech. Standards, data and talent are indispensable elements for driving the sound development of the climate finance ecosystem, and their establishment relies on the efforts and cooperation of different sectors. To this end, the HKMA collaborates with other relevant government departments, regulatory authorities, academic institutions and the financial industry, primarily through the Steering Group, to expand these elements. In addition to the development of the local green classification framework mentioned above, the Steering Group also promotes capacity building in the industry and improves Hong Kong's data resources through the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance established under it. Furthermore, the Steering Group has made good progress in other areas such as mandatory climate-related disclosures and carbon market opportunities. In 2022, the HKMA further strengthened the Exchange Fund's work in responsible investment, in particular setting a target for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. At the same time, we also enhanced our risk management work to improve the Exchange Fund's climate resilience and risk-adjusted long-term returns. In addition, to fully capture the opportunities that climate change may bring, we are committed to promoting the Exchange Fund's sustainable investments, seeking investment opportunities that help support climate transition and mitigate climate change, so as to enhance the long-term return of the investment portfolio. At the end of 2021, the weighted average carbon intensity of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio had dropped by 43% compared to the 2017 level. In fact, the Exchange Fund's exposure to carbon-intensive assets has consistently remained lower than that of the overall market. Looking ahead, we will continue to move towards the net-zero target by continuously strengthening the integration of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) factors into the investment management process, actively exercising asset ownership, continuously collaborating with various stakeholders, and focusing on the decarbonisation and transition of the investment portfolio. Within the HKMA, the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, which I chair, is responsible for formulating the HKMA's sustainability strategy. Our strategic direction is based on three main pillars: environment, staff and social responsibility. On the environment front, we are committed to promoting a green working environment and advocating a more environmentally friendly market to the public; on the staff front, as a responsible and caring employer, we actively foster a healthy and inclusive working environment; and on the social responsibility front, we are dedicated to enhancing public financial literacy, promoting financial inclusion, and actively giving back to society. Compared to the levels when we started tracking our carbon footprint in 2015, our per capita greenhouse gas emissions, energy consumption and paper consumption in 2022 all achieved double-digit percentage reductions. More importantly, we have formulated a roadmap to achieve net-zero emissions by or before 2050. In the short term, our target is to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions and, using 2015 as the baseline, reduce Scope 2 emissions by 63% by or before 2030. Addressing climate change and promoting sustainable development require continuous efforts and collaboration from multiple parties. On this important global issue, we understand that we must walk the talk, lead by example, and work together with like-minded peers and international organisations. In the next section, we will outline the HKMA's short-term plans and priorities in addressing climate change across its major functions. Achieving net-zero emissions by or before 2050 is a formidable task, and we will go all out to achieve this goal. We are confident that with the joint efforts of all our colleagues, the financial industry and the public, we will be able to successfully tackle the climate challenges ahead. Chief Executive, Eddie Yue

In 2023, the HKMA will continue to promote the sustainable development of Hong Kong's financial industry and fulfill its responsibilities as a responsible investor and a sustainable organization. At the same time, through participation in international and regional organizations, the HKMA will also strive to promote the broad development and best practices of green and sustainable finance. As the regulator of the banking industry, we will strive to strengthen the climate resilience of the banking sector and further enhance our green finance ecosystem to support banks' green transition. Specifically, the HKMA will engage with banks to understand their progress in implementing supervisory requirements on climate risk management, incorporate climate factors into our supervisory review process, and revise the Common Assessment Framework on the "Greenness Baseline" of the banking sector. Meanwhile, the HKMA will support banks in their efforts to enhance climate resilience and risk management capabilities, such as exploring different measures and technological solutions to help banks identify, measure, and monitor their climate risk exposures. The HKMA will also work with banks to launch the next round of climate risk stress testing as part of the regular supervisor-driven stress testing for 2023 to 2024. Participating banks will be required to assess their climate risk resilience under an enhanced stress testing framework, which covers multiple stress scenarios including extreme weather and adverse economic environments. To promote the healthy development of banks in providing green and sustainable investment products, the HKMA will keep abreast of local and international market and regulatory developments, maintain communication with the industry, and provide guidance on the selling process in due course. We will also conduct off-site thematic reviews to gain a comprehensive understanding of the green and sustainable investment products offered by banks. At the same time, to strengthen the building of the green finance ecosystem to support the green transition of the financial industry, the HKMA is planning to consult the industry on the structure and core elements for developing a local green classification framework. On market development, to promote Hong Kong as a regional green and sustainable finance hub, the HKMA will assist the Government in expanding the issuance size of green bonds under the Government Green Bond Programme and broadening the scope of the Programme to cover sustainable bonds; while attracting more green financing activities to Hong Kong through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme. The HKMA is also assisting in the implementation of the Government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme to expand Hong Kong's green finance talent pool. In addition, the HKMA will continue to encourage more Mainland local governments, institutions, and enterprises to conduct green financing through Hong Kong, and explore the feasibility of integrating green finance and technology. On the other hand, we will continue to collaborate with other agencies and departments through the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group on cross-sectoral issues such as capacity building and data, green taxonomy, climate-related disclosures and sustainability reporting, as well as carbon market opportunities. Through the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks, the HKMA will jointly launch various targeted initiatives with the International Finance Corporation in the Asian region, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market insights, offering targeted professional training for banks, and providing practical guidance to help banks develop roadmaps for making green finance a core business. Looking ahead, the Alliance will work closely with its cornerstone members, global partners, and knowledge partners to launch a membership program to expand the Alliance's influence in the Asian region. At the same time, the Alliance will also step up efforts to enhance the professional capacity of industry practitioners, promote green finance knowledge sharing, and lead the launch of project initiatives in new areas. As a responsible investor, the HKMA has set a target for the Exchange Fund investment portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by or before 2050, as its commitment to participating in global climate efforts and implementing the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures. Looking ahead, the HKMA will continue to incorporate Environmental, Social and Governance factors into its investment management process, strive towards the net-zero emissions target, and fully support global climate efforts. As a responsible and sustainable organization, the HKMA cares about its staff as well as the general public and the surrounding environment. We have formulated a sustainability roadmap and set climate targets for our own operations as our commitment to participating in global decarbonization and climate efforts. The HKMA will continue to prioritize the reduction of carbon emissions and encourage staff to fully support energy conservation and waste reduction. In addition, we will provide further guidance to staff to incorporate sustainability principles into the procurement process. To implement digital transformation and enhance operational agility, the HKMA will explore ways to modernize internal systems and applications to further improve work efficiency, while minimizing potential risks that may arise during the digital transformation process as much as possible.

Climate change is a major risk facing the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening the Hong Kong financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related issues in their daily business operations. To continue performing their vital functions in the financial system and to channel more capital towards green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risks. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places special emphasis on building banks' capacity to address and manage climate risks, and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. The HKMA also supports banks in enhancing their capabilities to detect environmental crimes and participated in the recently published Hong Kong Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment, which covers areas such as environmental crimes and illegal wildlife trade. In 2022, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee)1 issued the Principles for the effective management and supervision of climate-related financial risks and published responses to frequently asked questions to clarify how the existing Basel framework covers these risks. In response to these international developments, the HKMA will continue its efforts to integrate climate-related factors into the supervisory framework. Following the issuance of the Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" in 2021, the HKMA has maintained communication with banks to exchange views on the expectations, progress, and challenges in implementing the relevant supervisory requirements. To further strengthen the supervision of banks' climate risk management, the HKMA has formulated a two-year plan to integrate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process, which was communicated to the banking industry in June. As part of the implementation of the two-year plan, the HKMA issued the revised SPM module SA-1 "Risk-based Supervisory Approach" and enhanced the CAMEL2 rating system by incorporating climate risks into the risk-based supervisory process. Meanwhile, drawing on the experience gained from the 2021 pilot exercise, the HKMA refined the climate risk stress test scenarios and assessment framework. The HKMA also formulated plans to incorporate the next round of climate risk stress tests into the regular supervisor-driven stress testing, enabling a more comprehensive assessment of the banking sector's resilience under extreme climate scenarios. Under the two-year plan, the HKMA is also enhancing its Greenness Assessment Framework for banks to reflect the latest developments in sustainability-related issues, including climate risk management and transition planning. At the same time, the HKMA is reviewing the Supervisory Review Process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, aiming to encourage banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks to address risks associated with climate change and the transition to carbon neutrality. Given the growing popularity of green and sustainable products issued by banks, the HKMA conducted a round of thematic reviews focusing on banks' development and ongoing management of these products. The HKMA identified some good practices during the thematic reviews and issued a circular in December to share them with the industry, facilitating banks to progressively strengthen their climate risk management capabilities. The application of technology can improve data availability and enhance banks' capabilities in managing climate risks. The HKMA has commenced the development of a common platform for banks to assess the impact of physical risks on real estate. In addition, the HKMA, together with other central banks and supervisory authorities, completed a project under the BIS Innovation Hub to explore how technological solutions can assist in conducting physical risk assessments. The HKMA also attaches great importance to promoting sustainable and globally leading Anti-Money Laundering (AML) practices; this work adopts advanced analytics and Regtech, supplemented by fully automated supervisory data collection. Over the past 12 months, the HKMA has streamlined the AML supervisory data collection process to reduce the manual burden on banks and paper consumption. To enhance transparency across financial markets and align green finance policies, the HKMA collaborated with other financial regulators to develop a local green classification framework. The green classification framework, commonly known as a green taxonomy, classifies economic activities as green or sustainable, providing a reference for authorities and market participants to determine whether an activity or its related products are genuinely green or sustainable. To this end, the HKMA has maintained engagement with the industry and other relevant stakeholders to delve into the features and challenges of the framework, and is preparing to propose and consult on the structure and core elements of the framework in the first half of 2023. Deeply aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen ongoing surveillance. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its continuous monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analyses of climate-related risks in various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Workstream on Scenario Design and Analysis under the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helps further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and supervisors to better understand the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. In terms of research, the HKMA conducted several applied research projects in 2022, delving into two major topics: greenwashing behaviour in the corporate green bond market3, and the role of disclosure in mitigating climate risk exposures4. The findings of these studies help formulate policies and supervisory measures to address the impact of climate risks on financial stability. Locally, these studies help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risks on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA has shared the research findings with various stakeholders through multiple channels, including international central bank research conferences and the HKMA's Half-Yearly Monetary and Financial Stability Report. The HKMA's Liquidity Facilities Framework is a collateralised standby facility that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA is exploring the incorporation of sustainability considerations when assessing eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such participation, the HKMA helps facilitate international and regional policy dialogues on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draws insights to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a regional green and sustainable finance hub, the HKMA has stepped up efforts to enhance market awareness and participation, provide the necessary infrastructure and catalysts, and support international initiatives to align with global standards. The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the financial sector's responses to climate and environmental risks, accelerates the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supports the Government's climate strategies1. The Steering Group's work is primarily guided by its strategic plan, which sets out six key focus areas and five action points to strengthen Hong Kong's financial ecosystem for a greener and more sustainable future (Chart 1). Strengthening climate-related financial risk management to consolidate Hong Kong's position as a global risk management centre; Promoting the flow of climate-related information at all levels to facilitate risk management, capital allocation and investor protection; Enhancing the relevant skills of industry practitioners and raising public awareness and understanding; Encouraging product innovation and research initiatives to channel capital towards green and sustainable projects; Capitalising on the business opportunities presented by the Mainland to develop Hong Kong into a green finance centre in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA); Strengthening regional and international cooperation. Actions taken to advance Hong Kong's sustainable finance development to date: The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. The Steering Group's current work priorities include capacity building and data collection under the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance (see below), a green taxonomy (see "Developing a green classification framework to facilitate green capital flows" in the "Building a Sustainable Financial System" chapter on page 9), climate-related disclosures and sustainability reporting, and carbon market opportunities. Specifically, the Steering Group published a preliminary feasibility assessment of carbon market opportunities for Hong Kong in March, and will support the development of Hong Kong into a regional carbon trading centre, including developing a high-quality international voluntary carbon market and capitalising on opportunities arising from GBA cooperation. In December, the Steering Group announced a partnership with CDP2 to enhance data availability and sustainability reporting in Hong Kong. As part of this collaboration, the two parties developed a climate and environmental risk questionnaire targeting non-listed companies and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). This not only facilitates companies' sustainability reporting but also assists financial institutions in collecting and analysing company-level data for risk assessment and relevant business decisions. This is a significant step forward in expanding the coverage of the Steering Group's data work to include SMEs, a crucial segment of the economy that was previously difficult to reach. The Steering Group established the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance in July 2021 to coordinate the efforts of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders and academic institutions in capacity building and policy development, and to build a repository for resources and data. In the first half of 2022, the Centre launched three repositories focusing on data, training information and internship opportunities respectively, to help the financial industry and other sectors access data and learning resources related to green and sustainable finance. The resource repository provides data sources for assessing physical risks in Hong Kong. To facilitate industry talent training, the Centre assisted the Government in launching the "Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme" in December, providing subsidies to practitioners, students and graduates participating in green and sustainable finance-related training and upskilling. Other initiatives to promote capacity building include the launch of the "Sustainable Finance Internship Initiative" to create more internship opportunities for students, and the development of a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the HKMA's "Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners" for bank practitioners3. "Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme" The HKMA has also been actively supporting the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and the HKMA launched the "Alliance for Green Commercial Banks"4, bringing together financial institutions, banking industry associations, research institutions and innovative technology providers in the region to jointly develop a collaborative platform for green commercial banking. The Alliance aims to enable commercial banks and other financial institutions to fully unleash their potential in mainstreaming green finance as a core business, and to promote the financial system's participation in global climate change-related activities. Its operational approach is to provide a one-stop peer learning platform for financial institutions to acquire the necessary knowledge, tools and information to develop their own green finance roadmaps and transform into credible green financial institutions; to bring together green finance leaders and connect green financial institutions across different emerging markets; to facilitate communication and explore frontier issues; and to drive the global green finance agenda, unlocking endless green and climate-related investment opportunities. In June, five leading global financial institutions5 became cornerstone members of the Alliance, working closely with the IFC and the HKMA to encourage clients to adopt green strategies, promote best practices for green products and services, and unlock new business opportunities, thereby helping to achieve the transition to a green economy. In addition, three global partners and one knowledge partner6 committed in 2022 to providing climate expertise in areas ranging from innovation and standardisation to academic research. Details of the Alliance and its membership structure are available on the relevant webpage (English version): Cornerstone members, IFC and HKMA sign Memorandum of Understanding. On the other hand, since March 2021, the Alliance has hosted 18 training events and roundtables, attracting over 6,000 participants from across the globe, including the Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and the Americas. Furthermore, in June 2022, the Alliance, in collaboration with the Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (HKIMR)7, published its first frontier issue research report titled "Climate Risk: Definitions, Measurement, Current Practices and Regulatory Oversight". The HKMA has been promoting green and sustainable debt issuance and building a local ecosystem of related professional services. The total amount of green and sustainable debt (including bonds and loans) issued in Hong Kong in 2022 reached US$80.5 billion, representing a growth of 42%. +42% Green and sustainable debt issuance (US$80.5 billion) To demonstrate the Government's commitment to combating climate change, promoting green finance and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018, with the HKMA assisting in the implementation of the relevant green bond issuances. To date, the Government has issued green institutional and retail bonds totalling the equivalent of nearly US$16 billion, with the proceeds allocated to over 40 green government projects, including green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency and energy conservation. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the programme, the Government publishes a "Green Bond Report" annually, detailing the allocation of proceeds from green bonds and their expected environmental benefits. To enable the public to participate in Hong Kong's sustainable development through investment and share the fruits thereof, the inaugural batch of green retail bonds worth HK$20 billion was issued in May. It received enthusiastic support from the public and became the largest green retail bond issuance globally at the time. This issuance also expanded the variety of green and sustainable financial products in Hong Kong, consolidating Hong Kong's position as a premier green finance hub regionally and internationally. The Government also continued its regular green institutional bond issuance in the 2022-23 financial year, issuing the equivalent of US$5.75 billion in green bonds in January 2023. This triple-currency issuance covered US dollars, Euros and Renminbi, with tenors ranging from 2 to 30 years, continuing to provide an important benchmark for potential issuers in Hong Kong and the region. The issuance was well received by the global investment community and successfully attracted new investors who had not participated in the Government's previous green bond issuances, reflecting investors' strong confidence in Hong Kong's long-term credit fundamentals and economic underlying conditions. In response to investor demand, the Government doubled the issuance size of the Renminbi tranche to RMB 10 billion. The share of international investors and Mainland investors participating in this issuance through Southbound Trading under Bond Connect also increased, demonstrating Hong Kong's status as the premier offshore Renminbi business hub and further consolidating Hong Kong's leading position as an international financial centre. The HKMA also assisted the Government in issuing a tokenised institutional green bond in February 2023 to test the use of distributed ledger technology for bond issuance and settlement. This was the first tokenised green bond issued by a government globally. This primary issuance was settled on a T+1 basis on a private blockchain network, and subsequent processes (including coupon payments, secondary market trade settlement and maturity redemption) were also digitalised. The experience from this Government issuance can serve as a reference for market participants interested in conducting similar bond issuances in the future. To provide credible and accessible market information to the industry, the HKMA continued to collaborate with the Climate Bonds Initiative and the International Capital Market Association (ICMA) to publish annual reports on the green debt markets in Hong Kong and the region respectively. The ICMA report showed that Hong Kong became the largest hub for arranging international green and sustainable bonds in Asia in 2022, with the total amount of bonds arranged in Hong Kong reaching US$27.8 billion, accounting for over one-third of the regional total. The largest hub for arranging international green and sustainable bonds in Asia US$27.8 billion Following its inaugural issuance in 2021, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government issued another RMB 5 billion in offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong in November 2022, including RMB 2.6 billion in green and blue bonds8. In the same month, the Hainan Provincial People's Government also issued RMB 5 billion in offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, including blue and sustainable bonds. These bond issuance activities once again highlight Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating green and sustainable capital flows between the Mainland and the rest of the world, as well as its enduring status as the premier fundraising platform in the region. The HKMA continued to promote and administer the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" launched in 2021, leveraging the scheme to attract more relevant professional service providers (including financial institutions, green advisory firms and external reviewers) to establish and expand their presence in Hong Kong. The scheme has been well received by the industry. As of the end of 2022, the scheme had covered the pre-issuance, post-issuance or both external review service expenses for over 180 green and sustainable debt instruments, helping issuers ensure and demonstrate strict adherence to market best practices and international standards. Starting from March, the scheme was enhanced by lowering the minimum loan size threshold for applying for external review fee subsidies from HK$200 million to HK$100 million, facilitating smaller enterprises in obtaining green financing. Following the successful completion of the proof-of-concept for tokenised retail green bonds under Project Genesis in 2021, the HKMA and the BIS Innovation Hub Hong Kong Centre collaborated again under Genesis 2.0 to explore the technical feasibility of digitised carbon forwards (also known as Mitigation Outcome Interests, or MOIs), thereby enhancing the transparency, objectivity and environmental integrity of the green bond market. The project was completed in October 2022, successfully developing two prototypes that use blockchain and other related technologies to track, deliver and transfer digitised MOIs.

As one of the world's largest asset owners and managers, the HKMA plays an important role in promoting the development of green and sustainable finance to support the global climate change agenda. The HKMA is also a pioneer in responsible investment, having taken the lead in investing in green and sustainable assets as early as 2015. It requires its external investment managers to adopt the "Principles of Responsible Ownership" issued by the Securities and Futures Commission, and integrates environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "Capital Preservation First, Long-Term Growth", believing that emphasizing environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors can unlock long-term sustainable value for investments and mitigate related risks. Facing the increasingly severe challenges of climate change, the HKMA continues to advance on its responsible investment journey, including setting a "2050 net-zero emissions" target in 2022 and optimizing its risk management strategy to enhance the resilience of its asset portfolio, thereby striving for better risk-adjusted long-term returns for the Exchange Fund. The HKMA also actively participates in building a green and sustainable finance ecosystem, partnering with like-minded investors and regulators to jointly promote responsible investment, and collaborating with international organizations to formulate ESG investment standards. The transparency of climate-related information plays a pivotal role in managing climate risks. To fulfill its commitment to supporting the "Glasgow Declaration" published by the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) at the 2021 UN Climate Change Conference and to greening the global financial system, the HKMA makes climate-related disclosures for the Exchange Fund in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) under the Financial Stability Board.  a. Concrete evidence² continues to show that the impacts of climate change and related risks are significant. According to the latest report³ of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), even assuming that the "Nationally Determined Contributions" (NDCs) targets announced by various regions are fully implemented, it is estimated that the global temperature rise will still reach 2.1 to 2.4 degrees Celsius by 2100, making it difficult to achieve the Paris Agreement's goal of limiting the global average temperature increase to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. If regions adopt more aggressive policy measures to narrow the temperature gap, the resulting transition risks⁴ and the market's repricing of assets based on projected future trends, coupled with inherent physical risks, will exacerbate the pressure on asset valuations.  In light of the updates to the global warming trajectory and model assumptions, the HKMA leveraged the expertise of external consultants to further assess the resilience of the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" under a "Rapid Transition" scenario (Figure 2), in addition to the scenarios assessed in 2021. The "Rapid Transition" scenario incorporates higher transition risk factors in the short, medium, and long term, assuming that policy changes and technological developments jointly drive a rapid decline in carbon emissions, while various assets are subject to sudden divestment to keep the average temperature rise within 1.5 degrees Celsius by 2100. This scenario is broadly in line with the disorderly scenario recommended by the NGFS for forward-looking climate impact assessments.  The "Investment Portfolio" can remain resilient in the medium to long term, as a larger proportion of its asset allocation consists of sovereign bonds, which are less sensitive to transition impacts. Sector distribution is key. Low-carbon electricity and renewable energy assets can benefit from the relevant transition. Transition risks and asset repricing may cause shocks to performance (especially equity assets) in the short term. The "Investment Portfolio" as a whole will suffer increasingly severe impacts from physical risks that gradually emerge over time. Energy and traditional utilities remain the most vulnerable sectors.  Climate scenario analysis, like other modeling approaches, has its limitations. The analysis is based on the market benchmark sector distribution at the strategic asset allocation level and does not consider the effects of active security selection within a sector. Deeper research shows that the investments within the "Investment Portfolio" are generally more resilient to transition shocks or suffer milder impacts compared to the market benchmarks of the strategic asset allocation. This result reaffirms that the HKMA's responsible investment focusing on combating climate change can enhance the resilience of the asset portfolio.  The trajectory of climate change remains uncertain, and scenario analysis methodologies will continue to evolve with improvements in data quality and policy developments. The HKMA will regularly review the relevant scenarios and optimize the assessments to more clearly confirm the Exchange Fund's resilience to climate change.  As a long-term investor, the HKMA fully understands the risks and opportunities that climate change can bring. The HKMA is committed to further expanding sustainable investments and seizing opportunities aimed at climate transition, mitigating climate risks, and enhancing the long-term returns of the asset portfolio. The HKMA continued its strong momentum in 2022, increasing its holdings of green, social, and sustainability bonds by another 50%. In terms of equity investments, the HKMA invested in active equity portfolios with a governance theme and adopted a decarbonization strategy for passive equity portfolios that tilts towards companies with low carbon emissions. In addition, the HKMA is exploring with the General Partners of the Exchange Fund's "Long-Term Growth Portfolio" to establish dedicated private equity portfolios to promote green and sustainable development in Asia (Figure 3).  Figure 3: Continuous implementation of measures to increase ESG investments  The HKMA has invested in a pan-African wind farm operator. In addition to producing clean energy, the operator also places great emphasis on social and natural biodiversity factors. Before the establishment of the wind farm, local villagers used poisoned bait to prevent predators from preying on their livestock, but this inadvertently endangered certain vulture species that are endangered. Livestock is an important asset for local villagers. To help villagers protect their livestock, the operator built livestock shelters within the wind farm to protect the livestock from natural predators. Furthermore, the operator employed a bird monitoring team to issue warnings when vultures are attracted by animal carcasses accidentally left by predators, so as to shut down the wind turbines and prevent the vultures from being struck by the blades. Reducing livestock predation brings a win-win situation: on the one hand, it safeguards the livelihoods of the villagers, and on the other hand, it reduces the instances of vultures being struck and killed by wind turbines, thereby protecting endangered species. The HKMA is committed to reducing its institutional carbon footprint with the aim of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, and contributing to Hong Kong's overall climate targets. While striving to promote environmental sustainability, the HKMA also fulfills its commitments to caring for the physical and mental well-being of its staff, encouraging financial inclusion, and discharging its social responsibilities. The HKMA is dedicated to conducting its daily operations in a responsible and sustainable manner. To this end, the HKMA puts the concept of sustainability into practice under the three pillars of environment, staff, and social responsibility (Diagram 1). The Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee is responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating and implementing its sustainability strategy. Chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, the Committee comprises three Deputy Chief Executives and representatives from the Risk Management and Compliance Department and the Corporate Development and Operations Department. It submits regular reports to the Governance Sub-Committee of the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee. Under the leadership of the Committee, various teams and working groups are responsible for planning and executing measures within their respective purviews. In 2022, the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee approved the climate targets for institutional operations and reviewed the transition roadmap for achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. During the year, the Committee continued to review the progress of the HKMA's green initiatives, including proposals to enhance the HKMA's sustainable procurement policies, procedures, and methodologies. Sustainability Governance Structure and the HKMA's Institutional Sustainability Journey. In recognition of the HKMA's commitment to caring for the environment, its staff, and the community at large, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service awarded the "15 Years Plus Caring Organisation Logo" to the HKMA for the 16th consecutive year.  The HKMA pays close attention to its institutional carbon footprint and has formulated internal "Green Office Guidelines" to manage the environmental impact of its operational processes. The HKMA has integrated environmental factors into the interior design, operation, and maintenance of its offices. In 2022, BEAM Plus awarded a Gold rating to the HKMA for certain renovated office areas. This is the second green building certification obtained, following the LEED Gold certification received in 2021. Awarded BEAM Plus Interiors Version 1.0 Gold rating.  The HKMA implements various energy-saving measures. In 2022, total Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions8 were 2,996.4 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) (1.7 tCO2e per capita), a decrease of 38.2% compared to 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to traditional waste, the HKMA also reduces electronic waste by adopting technical solutions such as server virtualization and private cloud infrastructure. In 2022, the HKMA engaged an external company for the first time to conduct a waste audit to analyze the composition of waste generated in the office. The audit revealed that food waste accounted for a significant portion of the total waste, prompting the HKMA to launch a food waste recycling programme (see "Enhancing Waste Management" on page 41). Figure 3 Non-hazardous Waste Intensity  The HKMA prioritizes waste reduction at the source and is committed to reducing, reusing, and recycling. In 2022, the HKMA engaged a company for the first time to conduct a waste audit to better understand the composition of waste in its daily operations (plastics, paper, metals, glass, wood, electronic products, etc.) and to provide recommendations for waste reduction. Based on the results of this audit, the HKMA launched a food waste recycling programme in November, setting up food waste collection bins in all pantries.
