The residues generated during the conversion process can also be made into compost for landscaping and agricultural production. In addition, recycling bins are placed at various locations in the office for easy access. The HKMA shares recycling tips with staff and pays closer attention to further improving the source separation of recyclables, as well as the points to note when handling recyclable items such as cardboard boxes, food containers, and beverage bottles. Furthermore, we continue to organize activities to raise staff's environmental awareness, explain waste management policies, and encourage staff to make good use of the recycling facilities in the office. Food waste collected daily is transported to the organic resources recovery centre. Recycling plastic items.  The HKMA operates two data centres (production and backup respectively). As they account for a major portion of the institution's overall energy consumption, the HKMA has adopted green designs and various energy-saving measures, including in-row cooling systems, light-emitting diode (LED) lighting equipment, and 24-hour monitoring of power usage effectiveness. Following the completion of a consultancy study on the green performance of the aforementioned data centres in 2022, the HKMA is preparing to implement recommendations to enhance overall energy efficiency. It has also begun preparations to obtain green data centre certification.  Recognizing the importance of building a sustainability culture, the HKMA regularly launches various programmes and activities to educate and encourage staff to develop sustainability-friendly habits and adopt green and digitalized working practices. The HKMA shares green living tips with staff, as well as annual office-wide energy and paper consumption statistics, to remind them to help address environmental issues at a personal level; staff are also encouraged to provide suggestions on sustainability matters. Led by a Senior Manager of the Administration Division, a focus group brings together staff from different departments to brainstorm ideas and specific measures to promote a green working environment. Members of the focus group also act as ambassadors when new green initiatives are rolled out.  The HKMA encourages the wider community to adopt more environmentally friendly practices and has introduced various measures to enhance the operational efficiency of the HKMA, the financial industry, and the overall economy, minimizing resource consumption. The HKMA's "Submission Through Electronic Transmission" (STET) system is a one-stop platform for banks to submit documents to the HKMA electronically, covering various periodic returns required to be submitted on a weekly, monthly, quarterly, or annual basis. Another system, "e-Delivery", is a secure electronic communication channel for the HKMA to issue information such as circulars and guidelines to banks. Both systems help save a significant amount of paper each year. In handling bank complaints and enforcement work, the HKMA has taken measures to support paperless document submission, allowing bank customers to lodge complaints through electronic channels and by filling out online forms. The HKMA is also developing a new generation of management information systems to facilitate complaint handling and the transition from paper-based to digital records. To reduce paper consumption, the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU)9 has adopted digital signatures in its daily communications with participants, including the issuance of circulars, account opening and termination letters, and replies to audit confirmations. Looking ahead, the CMU will continue to explore more green initiatives, including the adoption of automated electronic processes for internal and external communications.  The HKMA encourages the public to adopt electronic payment methods more widely as an alternative to cash and physical cheques by promoting the use of the Faster Payment System (FPS) and Stored Value Facilities (SVFs). Further information on the FPS and SVFs is set out in the "Hong Kong as an International Financial Centre" chapter of the HKMA Annual Report 2022. Distributing electronic laisee (e-laisee) is simple and convenient, and it reduces the use of physical laisee packets and banknotes, helping to promote sustainability in Hong Kong. To this end, the HKMA continues to actively promote on various social and traditional platforms, encouraging the public to distribute e-laisee via the FPS or other e-wallet services through online or mobile banking during the Lunar New Year. Major banks and e-wallet operators also organized various campaigns to attract users to use e-laisee, such as providing festive user interfaces, enhancing functions for greater convenience, and launching lucky draws or cash rebates. The HKMA promoting e-laisee on social platforms.  For members of the public who choose to distribute physical laisee during the Lunar New Year, the HKMA continues to encourage them to use "good-as-new notes", which are used but still crisp banknotes, for laisee. Good-as-new notes can reduce the need to print new banknotes, thereby minimizing the environmental impact. Feedback from the note-issuing banks indicates that the public has become increasingly receptive to good-as-new notes in recent years.  The Coin Collection Programme reflects the HKMA's efforts in promoting coin recycling. Coins collected through the programme are recirculated into the market to meet public demand, improving the efficiency of coin circulation and reducing the need for minting new coins. The programme features two Coin Carts, which have served over 1 million people to date, collecting a total of over 800 million coins with a total face value of approximately HK$1.3 billion. In 2022, about 78% of users chose to use part or all of their coin value to top up their SVF accounts. The HKMA has maintained its collaboration with the Hong Kong Council of Social Service, deploying Coin Carts to collect coins on flag days of non-governmental organizations in a dedicated effort to support social services. Coin counting machines on the Coin Carts.  Launched in 2014, the Coin Collection Programme is the world's first systematic coin collection scheme utilizing a mobile cart concept. Over the years, it has won multiple local and international awards, and its innovative and environmentally friendly approach to coin handling has been widely recognized. The programme features two Coin Carts, each equipped with two high-speed coin counting machines to collect coins exchanged by the public. Members of the public can choose to exchange their coins for banknotes, use them to top up their SVF accounts (such as Octopus cards or e-wallets), or donate them to The Community Chest for charity. In addition to collecting coins, the Coin Carts are also occasionally deployed for various educational activities (such as student visits).

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the climate targets ("Climate Targets") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The Climate Targets were formulated with reference to the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual ("SBTi Corporate Manual"). The objective of this verification exercise is to verify whether the Climate Targets were formulated with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. This verification exercise was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to provide an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the information. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. Based on the results of this verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: • The Climate Targets were formulated with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. Sham Siu Yan Lead Auditor Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2023 Verification Statement Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the 2022 environmental data ("2022 Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The 2022 Data includes the total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emission intensity, paper consumption intensity, and non-hazardous waste generated intensity and recycling rate for 2022, as well as the changes in these data compared to the 2015 levels. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emission data was compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol ("GHG Protocol") jointly published by the World Resources Institute ("WRI") and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development ("WBCSD"). The verification scope covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2022, and also covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison. The verification scope covers a total of 6 office and warehouse assets, with 4 offices at 1) Two International Finance Centre office, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 2 warehouses at 5) Roxy Industrial Centre and 6) Shing Lee Centre, located in Kwai Chung and Tsuen Wan respectively. The objective of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2022 Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the verification scope, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency examined representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 6 assets. This verification exercise was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to provide an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing the selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checking, and conducted reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanism, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the 2022 Data, and selecting representative data and information for checking. Relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the information. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team was not involved in the preparation process of the 2022 Data. Based on the results of this verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the 2022 Data and concludes that: • The 2022 Data is materially accurate and reliable; • The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Sham Siu Yan Lead Auditor Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2023

Scaling up and accelerating climate action has become the most pressing issue of our time. We are almost halfway through the critical decade for the climate crisis. We need to cut global carbon emissions by more than 40% in this decade to have a chance of limiting global warming to within 1.5 degrees Celsius. However, greenhouse gas emissions continue to hit record highs. The latest climate science indicates that the window to limit global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius is rapidly closing. The impacts of a 1.1-degree Celsius rise in temperature are already clearly felt by all—extreme weather events such as record-breaking heatwaves and droughts, severe flooding, and storms are occurring more frequently around the world, and with increasing severity. Hong Kong is no exception. Last September, following the strike of a fierce super typhoon, we were immediately hit by a once-in-a-century torrential rainstorm. Despite our robust infrastructure and rapid disaster response capabilities, the impact was still severe—widespread flooding, traffic disruptions, and damage to roads in multiple locations. All these serve as a stark reminder that decisive and aggressive climate action brooks no delay.  Asia faces particularly daunting challenges on the path to low-carbon transition, especially in balancing economic development and sustainability. We need credible transition strategies that can appropriately balance climate action with economic growth and social inclusion. This is by no means an easy task. Driven by rapid economic development and fast population growth in the region, its carbon emissions account for more than half of the global total. At the same time, the Asia-Pacific region, with its high population density and geographical location, is highly vulnerable to sea-level rise and extreme weather. Given the diverse stages of development among economies in the region, while the low-carbon transition will bring new opportunities to some, raising the necessary transition finance poses a massive challenge for others. Market estimates suggest that the Asia-Pacific region will require over US$3 trillion in low-carbon transition investment annually for the next 30 years. As an international financial centre, Hong Kong has both the capability and the responsibility to harness the power of finance to support the low-carbon transition across the Asian region.  As a banking regulator, market enabler, and responsible investor, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has been making significant efforts towards the sustainability agenda. You will learn about the various specific measures and initiatives launched by the HKMA over the past year in the chapters of this report. Furthermore, to strengthen the HKMA's internal governance structure and more effectively coordinate sustainability efforts across different functional areas, we established the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee last year. For details on the Steering Committee, please refer to the newly added chapter on "Sustainability Governance".  Hong Kong banks play a vital role in supporting Asia's transition to net-zero emissions. In addition to fulfilling our traditional role as a banking regulator by ensuring banks properly manage climate risks in our day-to-day supervision, we also act as an enabler to support the banking sector in financing the low-carbon transition. One example is the development of a green taxonomy framework to help banks and other financial institutions identify environmentally sustainable activities, thereby aligning their business decisions with global climate goals. We launched a prototype of the green taxonomy framework for consultation in May and are currently refining the framework based on the feedback collected during the consultation period. In addition, as there is a growing demand for higher quality and globally comparable sustainability disclosure information, the HKMA is working with other regulators to develop a clear roadmap for Hong Kong to adopt the disclosure standards issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board in June, which serve as a comprehensive global baseline for sustainability reporting.  The HKMA's role as an enabler is not limited to setting frameworks and rules; we are also committed to addressing the pain points faced by the industry. Currently, many banks find it difficult to conduct physical risk assessments due to data limitations. In view of this, the HKMA will shortly launch a cloud-based physical risk assessment platform. By simply inputting a property address, banks can assess the impact of physical hazards on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios, thereby helping them manage relevant climate risks.  As a major international financial centre and sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong has been playing a bridging role, channelling international investment into sustainable projects in Asia to support the region's low-carbon transition. In recent years, the total volume of international green and sustainable bonds arranged for issuance in Hong Kong accounted for more than one-third of the Asian market, maintaining a clear lead over other regions. It is particularly worth mentioning that the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government and the Hainan Provincial People's Government issued green and sustainable bonds in Hong Kong for the third and second consecutive year respectively in 2023, reaffirming Hong Kong's important role as a green gateway connecting the Mainland with the rest of the world.  The flourishing of sustainable bond activities in Hong Kong is partly attributable to the demonstration effect of the Government Green Bond Programme. Since 2019, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds totalling approximately US$25 billion to institutional and retail investors. We seize every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors, and distribution channels, laying the foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. Following the issuance of the world's largest retail green bond by a government in 2022, we issued the world's first tokenised government green bond in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed the second issuance of tokenised green bonds; denominated in four major currencies and issued in a digitally native format, these are the world's first multi-currency digital green bonds.  At the same time, we have proactively rolled out various measures to enhance the vibrancy and competitiveness of Hong Kong's sustainable finance ecosystem. This covers work in multiple areas, including capacity building, data enhancement, green FinTech, and transition finance. In terms of talent development in particular, we launched a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners in 2023, providing systematic training for banking practitioners to enhance their understanding and expertise in green and sustainable finance.  Transition finance is another key focus area of our work. It provides funding for decarbonisation activities in high-carbon-emitting and hard-to-abate sectors, preventing these sectors from failing to transition due to a lack of financial support. To support the robust development of transition finance, the HKMA will expand the local green taxonomy framework to cover transition activities. We will also expand the scope of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme, which provides subsidies to eligible bond issuers and borrowers, to include transition bonds and loans, thereby encouraging regional enterprises to raise transition capital in Hong Kong. Furthermore, we will strengthen communication and engagement with relevant stakeholders to attract private sector investment into sustainable projects that were previously difficult to finance, through public-private partnerships and blended finance models.  Some of the aforementioned work requires cross-sectoral collaboration and is primarily coordinated by the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission. Regional cooperation is equally important. In addition to our long-standing partnership with the International Finance Corporation on the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks, the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office also joined the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment and the Green Investment and Finance Partnership as a founding member in 2023. Moreover, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero has announced plans to establish a chapter in Hong Kong. Through these partnerships, we hope to promote capacity building and knowledge sharing, thereby supporting the channelling of capital into sustainable projects in the region and globally.  To drive new business development and knowledge exchange, the HKMA also helped organise the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week earlier this year, attracting over 1,600 participants from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including top decision-makers in the global business and financial sectors, to jointly discuss solutions for scaling up climate finance in the region and forge new partnerships in this regard.  Chief Executive Mr Eddie Yue delivering a speech at the Asia Pacific Climate Business Forum, a highlight event of the Hong Kong Green Week  As the manager of Hong Kong's official reserves and a major global asset owner, the HKMA leads by example as a responsible investor. Since 2015, the HKMA has been spearheading investment in green and sustainable assets, and gradually expanding the Exchange Fund's ESG and green asset portfolios in both public and private markets. In line with the target of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's Investment Portfolio by or before 2050, the HKMA added a new active global equity portfolio themed around sustainability and climate transition last year, while expanding the application of a bespoke low-carbon equity index to another public market asset portfolio. In addition, the green, social, and sustainability bonds prioritised by the HKMA for investment have outperformed their investment benchmarks, embodying the principle of "doing well by doing good". In the private market, we continue to pursue green-related investment opportunities and have become an anchor investor in two Asia-focused transition funds. At the end of 2022, the Weighted Average Carbon Intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio decreased by 6% and 46% compared to 2021 and 2017 levels respectively, and has consistently remained below the broader market level.  As a sustainable organisation, the HKMA will continue to strive for progress, formulating our sustainability goals and plans based on the three pillars of environment, staff, and social responsibility. Specifically, in our journey towards a low-carbon transition, the HKMA continuously strengthens our climate resilience by assessing our environmental performance and implementing various internal measures. These measures cover emission reduction, energy efficiency enhancement, and waste management, with the ultimate goal of fulfilling our commitment to achieving net-zero emissions by or before 2050. We have formulated plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions in the near term and are making good progress towards our medium-term target for Scope 2 emission reduction by 2030. To attract and retain top talent to perform the HKMA's various vital functions, in addition to green targets, the HKMA is also committed to promoting the physical and mental well-being of our staff. Furthermore, by collaborating with various stakeholders, we contribute to building a caring society by promoting financial inclusion, enhancing public financial literacy, and raising public awareness of financial fraud prevention.  The climate challenge is immense and exceptionally urgent. Economies around the world are advancing towards a more sustainable future, a process that is expected to bring massive changes to financing activities and asset allocation. This transition entails considerable potential risks, but it will also be accompanied by unprecedented opportunities. As a major global sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has a responsibility to take the lead in addressing these challenges. At the same time, we are well-positioned to ride this wave. The HKMA will fully support the industry in financing the low-carbon transition; continue to lead by example as a responsible investor and a sustainable organisation; and collaborate with like-minded peers to advance this critically important global agenda.  Eddie Yue, Chief Executive

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are of global concern. The HKMA’s objective in its sustainability work is to strive to play a leadership role through its own policies and operations, ensuring that the Hong Kong financial system and the HKMA itself are resilient to climate change risks, and supporting the transition to a more sustainable economic development. By actively participating in international and regional organisations, the HKMA will also dedicate efforts to participating in the formulation of regional and global green and sustainable finance policies and standards. As the banking regulator, the HKMA will further strengthen the banking sector's climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. Specifically, the relevant key priorities include: launching a new round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management practices and conducting a new round of consultation meetings as part of reviewing banks' progress in implementing climate risk management supervisory requirements; continuing the work on integrating climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review process; completing the second round of the industry-wide climate risk stress test, providing guidance to participating banks throughout the process, and sharing observations and lessons learned with the industry; to enhance sustainability disclosures, including collaborating with relevant local authorities to align relevant requirements with the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) Sustainability Disclosure Standards as the global baseline, and preparing for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's Pillar 3 framework on climate-related financial risks; and sharing guidance on best practices for transition planning with the industry. To promote the healthy development of banks in providing green and sustainable investment products, the HKMA will continue to keep abreast of local and international market and regulatory developments, and maintain contact with the industry to ensure that banks adopt appropriate selling procedures. In addition, the HKMA will also play the role of a facilitator, striving to promote the development of the green finance ecosystem and support banks in providing financing for economic transition. We will soon publish the local green taxonomy and continue to expand its coverage to include more activities such as transition activities. At the same time, we will also continue to explore the application of technological solutions to assist banks in identifying, measuring, and monitoring their climate risk exposures; one example is the upcoming launch of a cloud-based platform to facilitate banks' physical risk assessments. To enhance the professional competence of practitioners, we will also develop the Professional Level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking in 2024. Hong Kong is well-positioned as a regional and international sustainable finance hub. To leverage this role, the HKMA is assisting the Government in implementing the initiatives in the 2023-24 Budget to expand the scope of the Government Green Bond Programme to cover sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable bond market; while attracting more green financing activities, including transition finance activities, to Hong Kong through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme. We will also continue to encourage more governments, institutions, and corporates to raise green funds through Hong Kong, and explore the potential synergies between green finance and technology. Furthermore, we will continue to assist in the implementation of the Government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme to expand Hong Kong's green finance talent pool. As the Co-Chair of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other agencies and departments to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and initiatives aimed at promoting the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Steering Group will focus its work on three areas in 2024, including sustainability disclosures, the application of technology, and transition finance. As another key priority, through the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks, the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation will continue to jointly launch various targeted initiatives in the Asian region, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted professional training for banks, and providing practical guidance to assist banks in supporting financial institutions to establish their tailored green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also strive to deepen our collaboration with the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero, the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment, and the Green Investment and Finance Partnership. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving the net-zero emissions target for the Investment Portfolio of the Exchange Fund by 2050 or earlier. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund's investments through a three-pronged responsible investment approach, ensuring that the resilience of the asset portfolio is maintained in the journey towards net zero. We fully understand that achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement requires a transition of the real economy as a whole. Therefore, we are refining our net-zero strategy to focus on assets that can bring positive climate benefits to the real economy, while taking into account the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. As an environmentally friendly organisation, the HKMA's decarbonisation strategy will continue to keep pace with the times to reflect the latest market, regulatory, technological, and other climate-related developments. To further strengthen the HKMA's climate resilience and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of leveraging technological solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our offices. In addition, we will continue to actively encourage staff to participate in our sustainability efforts, including launching promotional campaigns to cultivate sustainable habits and optimising office processes and practices. Furthermore, the HKMA will continue to maintain consistent, highly efficient, and sustainable procurement practices, including assessing suppliers' ESG practices during selection and contract renewal. Building on the green data centre certification obtained in 2023, the HKMA is committed to upholding the specified certification standards. Regarding the regular upgrading of data centre facilities, in addition to keeping abreast of the latest technological developments, we will also incorporate green design and practices. At the same time, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the application of technology and convergence, and actively modernise internal systems to improve efficiency and minimise potential risks as much as possible. Finally, regarding social focus areas, the HKMA will identify more community service opportunities for colleagues, and collaborate with the industry to promote financial inclusion and enhance financial literacy, as well as raise public awareness of preventing financial fraud.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impact. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking supervisor, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainable organization, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across the Asian region. The HKMA has a robust sustainability governance framework in place to lead the formulation of its relevant strategies and policies; oversee the implementation of related measures; and ensure that sustainability factors are integrated into the HKMA's own operations and practices. In its commitment to practicing good corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency for its sustainability-related work. This governance framework ensures the effective integration of sustainability factors into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and features effective mechanisms to monitor and evaluate the progress and effectiveness of its sustainability efforts. The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant Sub-Committees, which are responsible for monitoring the HKMA's work, including its sustainability efforts, and providing advice; the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which is responsible for leading the HKMA's overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategies and policies at the management level; in terms of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and for other functional areas, relevant groups and working groups responsible for planning and executing sustainability measures related to banking and market development, as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the efforts of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA's various sustainability initiatives over the past few years, we established the Steering Committee in October as a new central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability efforts across different functional areas of the HKMA1. It provides guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans for ESG-related matters across four functional areas: banking, market development, Exchange Fund investment, and internal operations; oversees the implementation of ESG-related plans by various functional departments of the HKMA; evaluates the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG targets; and oversees external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with three Deputy Chief Executives serving as standing members. In addition, we invite Executive Directors responsible for key functions related to green and sustainability matters to attend the Steering Committee meetings to report on the major deliverables and future plans of their work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's banking departments, Corporate Development and Operations Department, External Department, and the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA and the SFC co-initiated the establishment of the Steering Group in May 20202. As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts regarding the financial industry's response to climate and environmental risks, with a view to consolidating Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For details of the Steering Group's work, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change is a major risk facing the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening the Hong Kong financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate targets and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related issues in their daily business operations. To continue performing their vital functions in the financial system and channel more capital towards green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risks. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places special emphasis on building banks' resilience to and capacity for managing climate risks, and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. The HKMA is committed to formulating various policy measures to enhance the banking system's resilience to climate risks. In August, the HKMA issued a circular on net-zero transition planning, setting out high-level principles to assist banks in maintaining safety and soundness during the economic transition to net-zero emissions. Following the issuance of the circular, we conducted a survey on selected banks in the fourth quarter to understand their transition planning practices. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices regarding transition planning with the industry, and will organize seminars or workshops to facilitate the exchange of experience among the industry. Regarding disclosure requirements, in response to the latest international developments, including the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards published in June and the consultation launched by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) in November on a Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks, the HKMA is stepping up its efforts to refine the sustainability-related disclosure framework for banks in Hong Kong. Specifically, the HKMA is collaborating with relevant local authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong to align with the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. During the year, the HKMA strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and provided recommendations to help banks further enhance their climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. The HKMA made significant progress in implementing its two-year plan to integrate climate risk factors into its banking supervisory processes. Climate risk management has now been included as a standing agenda item in prudential meetings with bank management. Bank supervisors also adopted the enhanced CAMEL rating system1, which has incorporated climate risk factors, to assess banks' risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of the implementation of the two-year plan to integrate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process, the HKMA revised the "Green" assessment framework to focus on banks' transition planning practices. The HKMA is also reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy levels and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, to encourage banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks against climate risks. A key focus under the two-year plan in 2023 was that, following the end of the 12-month implementation period for compliance with the Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) module GS-1 on "Climate Risk Management", the HKMA launched a round of thematic reviews on climate-related risk governance in the second quarter. The thematic review covered four major areas, including the governance structure for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategy, oversight of climate-related risk management, and corporate culture, awareness, and communication. The HKMA made several enhancements to the climate risk stress test framework, including the introduction of a new 5-year scenario to assess the potential impact on banks of concurrent economic and climate change shocks. Following these enhancements and as part of the HKMA's regular supervisor-driven stress testing programme, the second round of the climate risk stress test was launched in June to comprehensively assess banks' climate risk exposures and further enhance their capacity to manage climate risks. A total of 44 banks participated in this risk stress test, representing an increase of over 60% compared to the first pilot exercise in 2021. The HKMA also hosted a climate risk stress test forum in November, which was attended by up to 300 banking practitioners. By facilitating the sharing of experience among banks, this event helped deepen the industry's overall understanding of climate risk measurement. The HKMA also conducted a series of consultation meetings to review banks' progress in implementing the HKMA's SPM module GS-1 on "Climate Risk Management". The HKMA held meetings with bank management to discuss their work on climate risk management and the common challenges faced by the industry, and reviewed the information provided by banks and other public information to assess their relevant progress. The HKMA provided targeted recommendations to banks, encouraging and supporting them to continue strengthening their climate risk management capabilities in accordance with the HKMA's supervisory expectations. As the world increasingly focuses on climate change and strives to address related issues, the HKMA noted a growing demand for green and sustainable investment products, with some banks offering such products to meet customer needs. In view of this, the HKMA completed a thematic review on the sale of green and sustainable investment products by banks and issued a circular in November, setting out the standards expected of banks by the HKMA and sharing observed good practices. This circular covers various areas including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and controls, staff training, and bookbuilding, aiming to mitigate potential greenwashing risks and enhance investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of such investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The HKMA is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For example, technology can improve data availability and risk analytics, strengthening banks' capabilities to manage climate risks. The HKMA will soon launch a pilot version of a cloud-based platform for banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. In addition, the HKMA continues to collaborate with other central banks and supervisory authorities to explore how technology solutions can assist in conducting physical risk assessments. On the other hand, the HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable anti-money laundering (AML) practices through the application of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence, reducing the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the HKMA launched a shared online data submission platform to fully automate the financial crime risk data collection process, thereby enhancing banks' workflows for submitting AML-related data in a sustainable manner. In September, the HKMA organized the "Green Fintech Competition", aiming to seek market-ready solutions to help the banking industry address challenges in the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability or climate-related disclosures and reporting. The competition attracted over 85 submissions from around 70 companies. In December, the HKMA hosted the "Green and Sustainable Banking Conference", providing a platform for the banking and technology sectors to explore the roles of low-carbon technology and green fintech in the net-zero transition of Hong Kong and the Mainland, and concurrently announced the results of the "Green Fintech Competition". This event attracted about 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulatory authorities, and academia. To enhance transparency across financial markets and bring greater consistency to green and sustainable finance decision-making, the HKMA, with the assistance of a consultancy firm, developed a local green classification framework. In May, the HKMA published a discussion paper on the "Prototype of a Green Classification Framework for Hong Kong" to seek stakeholders' views on the development and implementation of a green taxonomy. Based on the consultation results, the HKMA is fine-tuning the prototype framework and identifying other areas for the next phase of framework development. The HKMA participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF); the FATF has identified environmental crimes as a predicate offence for money laundering, and given the interconnectedness between AML and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG), this area is receiving increasing attention from more regulatory authorities. Deeply aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its ongoing surveillance work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its continuous monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analysis of climate-related risks in its various financial stability reports. By actively participating in the Workstream on Scenario Design and Analysis under the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helps further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and supervisors to better understand the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board (FSB), the HKMA participates in analyzing the interplay between the transition planning of financial and non-financial firms and financial stability, enabling policymakers to form a forward-looking and dynamic perspective in examining climate-related financial risks. Regarding research work, the HKMA conducts various applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial sector and the economy. Research topics include the climate risk exposures of the banking sector and investment funds2, ESG fund flows3, the impact of climate change on property prices4, and the ripple effects of corporate ESG performance in global supply chains5. The above research findings enhance the HKMA's understanding of the impact of climate change and ESG issues on financial stability, facilitating the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, these studies help strengthen the HKMA's continuous monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risks on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA also shares its research findings with a broad range of stakeholders through various channels, such as international events on climate-related matters and the HKMA Research Memorandums. The HKMA's "Liquidity Facilities Framework" is a collateralised standby facility arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations when assessing eligible collateral under this framework in accordance with NGFS recommendations. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such participation, the HKMA helps facilitate international and regional policy dialogues on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draws insights from them to help strengthen the climate resilience of the Hong Kong financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. During the year, the HKMA worked closely with local and international partners to build a richer ecosystem and promote the further development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group) coordinates the financial sector's responses to climate and environmental risks, accelerates the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supports the Government's climate strategies. The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced key initiatives to support Hong Kong in capitalizing on sustainable finance opportunities, with major work areas including sustainability disclosures, ecosystem enhancement, transition finance, and green FinTech. Specifically, the Working Group on Sustainability Disclosures was established to formulate a roadmap for Hong Kong's adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. The roadmap will comprise four key areas, including sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, and capacity building. In addition, the Working Group on Transition Finance was set up to explore ways to support financial institutions and corporates in their transition planning and reporting. The Steering Group also enhanced the sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sector capacity building and data enhancement. Particularly on data, we continued to promote the adoption of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies 2, launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Steering Group will continue to keep abreast of the latest developments in the green and sustainable finance space and elevate Hong Kong's position as a regional and global green and sustainable finance hub. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced three new key initiatives to capture the investment and financing opportunities arising from the Asia-Pacific region's low-carbon transition. To facilitate capacity building in the industry, the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance under the Steering Group administers the Government's Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme, which provides subsidies to practitioners, students, and graduates who undertake training and acquire qualifications related to green and sustainable finance. As of December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training programmes or qualifications were registered as eligible under the Scheme, and over 560 subsidy applications were approved. The HKMA also launched the Core Level of the new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners. This module aims to foster talent development in the banking industry and enhance the overall professional competence of practitioners. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the banking industry to develop the Professional Level of the module to meet the industry's rapidly growing demand for green and sustainable finance professionals. To help financial institutions and corporates, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), better understand key climate and sustainability-related issues, including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions calculation, and transition planning, the HKMA collaborated with relevant Government bureaux and departments, as well as global partners such as CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ)3, and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF)4, to organize a series of seminars and thematic workshops during the year, attracting participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. For students, following the launch of the Sustainable Finance Internship Scheme in 2022, training sessions were held in January and February 2023 to deepen the understanding of sustainable finance among interns and university undergraduate alumni. Recognizing the potential of technology in bridging climate-related data gaps and improving data quality, the HKMA is committed to making such data more accessible and enhancing its quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group rolled out a series of website enhancements to provide a one-stop source of green and sustainable finance information for financial institutions, corporates, and the public. Key enhancements include a sustainability disclosure e-Portal, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and estimation tools, and more centralized, easy-to-navigate, and searchable data and resources. During the Hong Kong Green Week, the Steering Group also co-organized the "Catalysing Sustainable Finance with Technology" event with Cyberport and InvestHK to showcase leading green innovative solutions and Hong Kong's strengths in green technology. The "Hong Kong Green Week – Finance Stream" was held from 26 February to 1 March 2024, during which various sustainability-themed events attracted over 1,600 participants from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including representatives from financial institutions, corporates, central banks, international organizations, government agencies, academia, and consulting firms. The flagship event of the Hong Kong Green Week was the Climate Business Forum: Asia Pacific, co-hosted by the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation (IFC). The Forum brought together over 400 guests, including top decision-makers in global business and finance, to discuss solutions for unlocking climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. The two-day event explored a wide range of topics, including energy transition, heavy industry decarbonization, circular economy, the future of sustainable finance, and new climate technologies in emerging and developing markets in the Asia-Pacific region. The Forum received strong responses from public and private sector organizations, which co-hosted over 10 roundtables, seminars, and other networking events. Topics covered climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, net-zero transition financing, green finance taxonomies, and green development financing in the Belt and Road regions. In addition, the HKMA and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) co-hosted the Asia Climate Finance Roundtable on 29 February 2024 to explore key measures for scaling up climate finance and the roles of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. The aforementioned events are part of the HKMA's overall efforts to promote and enrich Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance ecosystem, serving as useful platforms to help participants drive new business development, share knowledge, and explore new opportunities to address climate finance challenges in the Asia-Pacific region. The HKMA has also been actively supporting the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, the IFC and the HKMA launched the "Alliance for Green Commercial Banks" 5 as a collaborative platform bringing together financial institutions, banking industry associations, research institutions, and innovative technology providers in the region to jointly develop green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has held 22 capacity building events and roundtables, attracting over 7,300 participants from across the globe, including the Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. In October, the Alliance, in collaboration with Crédit Agricole CIB, published its second thought leadership report titled "Developing an Ambitious Green Banking Climate Strategy: A Case Study". The Alliance and Crédit Agricole CIB jointly published the thought leadership report "Developing an Ambitious Green Banking Climate Strategy: A Case Study" in October. During the year, the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office (IFFO) joined the newly established Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment (CASI) and the Green Investment and Finance Partnership (GIFP) initiated by the Belt and Road Initiative International Green Development Coalition. The collaboration with CASI and GIFP will facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing, and channel more capital into green and sustainable projects in Asia and the broader region. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the launch of its Hong Kong Chapter, which will help support the net-zero efforts of financial institutions in Hong Kong and the Mainland. The HKMA assists the work of GFANZ in an advisory capacity. To demonstrate the Government's commitment to combating climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and livable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. The HKMA assists in the issuance of green bonds under the Programme. To date, the Government has issued institutional and retail green bonds totaling the equivalent of around US$25 billion, with the proceeds allocated to over 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Programme, the Government publishes the Green Bond Report annually, detailing the allocation of green bond proceeds and their expected environmental benefits. The Government continued its regular institutional green bond issuances in the 2023-24 financial year, issuing the equivalent of around US$6 billion in green bonds in June. This triple-currency offering comprised US dollar, euro, and Renminbi (RMB) bonds across various tenors, attracting different types of investors with an overwhelming response, recording an equivalent of nearly US$30 billion in subscription amounts. Among them, the issuance size of the RMB bonds was increased from RMB 10 billion issued in January to RMB 15 billion, and a 10-year RMB bond was introduced for the first time, helping to extend the Government's RMB yield curve and further enrich the offshore RMB product offerings. The enthusiastic response from global investors to the Government's green bond issuances reflects their recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the Government issued the second batch of retail green bonds totaling HK$20 billion, further facilitating market development and promoting financial inclusion. This issuance provided the public with an investment opportunity offering stable returns, allowing them to participate in and benefit from the development of green finance in Hong Kong.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA plays a crucial role in promoting the development of green and sustainable finance to support the global climate agenda. The HKMA has always been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, the HKMA has been spearheading investments in green and sustainable assets, requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise asset ownership, and integrating environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. Investing prudently in accordance with the principle of "capital preservation first, long-term growth"1, the HKMA believes that paying adequate attention to ESG factors helps mitigate relevant investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and set a "2050 net-zero emissions" target2 for its "Investment Portfolio", the HKMA is committed to continuously advancing its responsible investment journey, emphasizing sustainability, particularly the pressing issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and striving for better risk-adjusted long-term returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA participates in building a robust green and sustainable finance ecosystem, partnering with like-minded investors, regulators, and international organizations to jointly develop industry operational standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment in the financial industry and the central banking community. Through steering and collaborative initiatives, the HKMA is dedicated to fostering a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand.   Chart 1 The Exchange Fund's Responsible Investment Journey   Comprehensive and reliable ESG information is essential for integrating sustainability and planning a credible climate transition to achieve the net-zero target. To fulfill its commitment to supporting the Glasgow Declaration3 of the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) and the strategic plan of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, the HKMA leads by example and has prepared this chapter on the Exchange Fund's responsible investment in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD).   The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee (EFAC), chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The primary guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practice responsible investment while taking into account the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee (IC) under EFAC, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring the ESG and climate-related risks involved in the Exchange Fund's investments. The IC reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors their implementation through regular meeting reports from the Sustainable Investment (SI) team of the EFIO. As shown in Chart 2, the ESG Committee under the EFIO, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and monitoring various ESG initiatives within the EFIO. The initiatives and work progress discussed at the quarterly meetings of the ESG Committee are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the EFIO. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Strategy Officer of the EFIO, meets semi-annually to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the EFIO, to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG objectives.   Chart 2 Responsible Investment Governance Structure of the EFIO   As shown in Chart 1, the EFIO embarked on its responsible investment journey in 2016, with an initial focus on managing ESG risks that could affect the financial performance of the Exchange Fund. As sustainable development rapidly evolves and transcends risk considerations to become a strategic priority for major institutions worldwide, the EFIO has reviewed its approach to responsible investment. July 2023 marked another milestone with the establishment of a new Business Strategy division within the EFIO, led by the Chief Strategy Officer. This division is responsible for coordinating and leading the strategic development of the EFIO and incorporates the dedicated responsible investment team formerly under the Risk Management and Compliance Division—now known as the Sustainable Investment (SI) team. This strategic move reflects the HKMA's elevation of its responsible investment focus from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing sustainability-related matters in investments. The SI team works closely with different teams within the EFIO on the integration of ESG factors and assists the senior management of the EFIO in managing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across various asset classes:   Public market investments — The Credit, Rules and Compliance Committee, comprising senior management of the EFIO, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to the advice of the SI team, and monitors the ESG profile of the fixed income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Compliance Division. In addition, the SI team participates in the selection, appointment, and monitoring process of external investment managers for the equity portfolio from an ESG perspective (for details, please refer to the section "Promoting Active Asset Ownership" under "Risk Management" on page 40). The HKMA understands that physical and transition risks4 brought about by climate change, as well as related opportunities, will affect the long-term performance and value of the Exchange Fund's investments. The "Emissions Gap Report 2023"5 published by the United Nations Environment Programme projects that unless global greenhouse gas emissions are further reduced, the global average temperature will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels by 2030. The urgent need for more aggressive policies, technological developments, or behavioral changes to control temperature rise may exacerbate transition risks such as asset devaluation or stranded asset shocks. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also pose additional physical risks to investments. The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places special emphasis on climate-related factors when integrating ESG factors. The HKMA in 2022 set a target for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by or before 2050, further demonstrating its commitment to the global climate agenda. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three-pronged approach with a clear focus on decarbonization and transition. The following sections will detail these approaches.   Chart 3 The HKMA's Three-Pronged Approach to Responsible Investment   In the journey towards the net-zero target, the HKMA prefers proactive engagement over exclusion or divestment from its investable universe. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial to achieving the primary investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially impacting investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies that are undergoing transition and possess excellent technology and good corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including those in high-emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding relevant investments or divesting does not help solve the carbon emission problem. Instead, by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising asset ownership to support these industries, the HKMA drives them to implement transitions towards sustainable and low-carbon operational practices, thereby bringing beneficial changes to themselves and the world. In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net-zero investment strategy, adopting a comprehensive approach to strive for transition outcomes that align with the Exchange Fund and global net-zero targets, while adhering to its guiding principles for responsible investment.   By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities to facilitate climate transition and enhance the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's asset portfolio (Chart 4). The HKMA's responsible investment maintained good momentum in 2023. Furthermore, the green, social, and sustainability bonds prioritized by the HKMA outperformed their investment benchmarks, demonstrating the philosophy of "doing well by doing good." In the private markets, the HKMA actively builds a resilient Long-Term Growth Portfolio, seizing investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic megatrends such as climate and energy transition. For example, during the year, the HKMA invested in two Asia-focused transition investment funds, reflecting the HKMA's commitment to addressing Asia's climate transition needs. The HKMA is committed to becoming a sustainable organisation, taking a multi-pronged approach to reduce its carbon footprint with the target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA also focuses on the physical and mental well-being of its staff and social responsibility, and strives to promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy. As a responsible organisation, the HKMA sets sustainability goals under the three pillars of environment, staff, and social responsibility. Established in October, the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee) 1, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the primary decision-making body for various corporate sustainability initiatives. The predecessor of the Steering Committee was the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, which was responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating the vision, strategies, and policies for corporate sustainability and social responsibility matters. At the departmental level, the Executive Director (Corporate Development and Operations) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and regularly submits progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Team provide support in coordinating corporate sustainability efforts; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming on how to create a green working environment, while the latter aims to foster a culture of participating in volunteer activities. The HKMA has formulated a roadmap to guide its transition path. The focus is on implementing decarbonisation strategies in its daily operations, including operating green buildings and data centres, practising green travel, adopting energy-saving measures, digital tools and greener operating models, reducing waste, and building a sustainability culture. The HKMA also plans to utilise carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and adopt carbon offsetting measures for hard-to-abate emissions. In addition to the above environmental commitments regarding its daily operations, the HKMA continues to roll out greener operating solutions for the wider community, ranging from channels for banks to submit electronic documents and communicate, to electronic payment and coin collection programmes for the general public. To strengthen and sustain its operational capabilities, the HKMA employs a professional workforce, builds a talent pool, and focuses on the physical and mental well-being of its staff. In terms of social responsibility, the HKMA encourages staff to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; considers engaging social enterprises (SEs) in procurement; promotes financial consumer education; and collaborates with the banking industry to ensure fair access to basic banking services for all segments of society. The remainder of this chapter sets out the details of the above strategies. Under the HKMA's overarching corporate risk management framework, the Risk Committee 2, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. The physical impacts of climate change, such as more extreme weather causing flooding or other damage, may affect the HKMA's offices and hinder staff commuting. To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its business continuity plan to cope with extreme weather conditions. The HKMA also conducts regular evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to execute business continuity measures. The design of the offices also incorporates various measures to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the HKMA's energy use, air travel, and waste management. The HKMA has been monitoring its exposure to transition risks by tracking its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, waste generation, as well as energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's climate target is to achieve net-zero GHG emissions for Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 (air travel) across all areas of its corporate operations by 2050 or earlier. As a near-term emission reduction target, the HKMA plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions by replacing all of its existing vehicles with electric vehicles; and to reduce Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier, using 2015 as the baseline year, through various decarbonisation and offsetting strategies. Despite the challenges in determining Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will continue to take a multi-pronged approach to minimise Scope 3 GHG emissions (such as paper consumption, waste generation, and air travel) as far as practicable. The HKMA's long-term and near-term emission reduction targets were formulated with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) methodology, which has also been verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA). The HKMA has appointed the HKQAA to verify its emissions, energy and paper consumption, and waste data disclosed in this report 6. The verification scope and criteria are set out in the "Verification Statement" section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing the Annual Report 2022, the HKMA also published its standalone Sustainability Report 2022 for the first time. The HKMA's efforts in enhancing ESG reporting were recognised, winning the ESG Award in the "Public Sector Category" at the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023". The HKMA is the first financial regulator to win an award in this category. The judging panel commended the HKMA for achieving good ESG standards, noting that the Sustainability Report was clear and easy to read, and that the appointment of an independent body to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report reflected its commitment to highly transparent and accountable reporting. Furthermore, the HKMA received the highest rating of Gold Award in the "Non-profit Making and Charitable Organisations" category at the Hong Kong Management Association's "2023 Best Annual Reports Awards". The judging panel praised the HKMA's annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial information and making good use of infographics, demonstrating the HKMA's determination to enhance financial literacy and promote financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA's commitment to caring for the environment, its staff, and the community at large, The Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the "15 Years Plus Caring Organisation" logo to the HKMA for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to properly managing the environmental impact caused by its operations. Its internal Green Office Guidelines provide guidance to staff on resource utilisation and office waste generation. The HKMA has integrated environmental factors into the design, operation, and maintenance of its owned and leased offices. When renovating offices, existing furniture and fitting-out materials are reused as much as possible to reduce waste, and priority is given to environmentally friendly building and decorative materials. The HKMA has consistently adopted this practice, and as a result, was awarded Gold certifications under LEED 7 and BEAM Plus Interiors 8 in 2021 and 2022 respectively for parts of its renovated offices in Two International Finance Centre. Enhancing energy efficiency through the adoption of new technologies and the optimal use of existing technologies remains one of the HKMA's key focuses. In addition to promoting good habits, such as switching off unnecessary lighting in work areas outside office hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include the use of light-emitting diode (LED) lighting, motion sensors, setting air-conditioning room temperatures at appropriate levels, and optimising energy use in the IT network infrastructure. The HKMA's energy consumption has continued to decrease, standing at 2.59 MWh per capita 9 in 2023, a drop of 29.7% compared to the 2015 baseline (Chart 1). Given the nature of the HKMA's daily operations, its GHG emissions primarily stem from the consumption of electricity generated by fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuels and electricity was 1.48 tCO2e per capita 10, a decrease of 45.2% compared to 2015 (Chart 2). In addition to standardising equipment, office software, and meeting facilities, the HKMA has adopted digital tools and technologies, and automated and streamlined workflows to build a digitalised working environment and enhance online collaboration within the organisation. 11 Paperless meetings have become the primary mode of meeting at the HKMA. To further reduce paper consumption and improve efficiency, various internal administrative matters primarily adopt electronic processes. Furthermore, the HKMA encourages staff to integrate into green and digitalised working modes, replacing paper documents and communications with digital alternatives. Meanwhile, the implementation of an electronic record-keeping system is also underway. The aforementioned green and digitalised measures have yielded positive results. The HKMA's paper consumption intensity in 2023 was 11.55 kg per capita, a significant decrease of 64.8% compared to 2015 (Chart 3). As most international events have resumed in physical formats following the COVID-19 pandemic, and to promote the development of Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre, it is inevitable that relevant HKMA staff need to travel overseas for business. To reduce carbon emissions caused by air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to take direct flights or combine different business trips where practicable when participating in overseas events. At the corporate level, the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO2e in 2023 through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. In addition, the HKMA participated in a Gold Standard 12 certified carbon offsetting programme to offset the remaining carbon emissions caused by air travel; the programme involves waste-to-energy, solar power generation, and the provision of efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue to make similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA's procurement process takes sustainability and environmental factors into consideration. As part of a comprehensive review of the organisation's procurement policies and procedures, the current practice of purchasing green products has been formalised, complying with the environmental specifications of the Government's "Green Procurement List", particularly in the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables.
