Furthermore, ESG factors and innovative proposals that help enhance productivity and efficiency have been incorporated into the tender evaluation criteria. At the same time, all suppliers are required to commit to complying with environmental regulations. In accordance with the "4R" principles, namely Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle, the HKMA adopts a three-pronged approach to minimise waste generation and manage waste disposal. In addition, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. Details of the non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various types of recyclable waste, are set out in the "Performance Summary" section on page 56. In 2023, the HKMA directly participated for the first time in the red packet recycling programme organised by the building management company of the International Finance Centre offices. Staff handed in a total of approximately 3,000 used but still intact and pristine red packets. These red packets were subsequently handed over to an environmental organisation for distribution to the public for use in the coming Lunar New Year. Given that the HKMA's operational and backup data centres account for a major portion of the organisation's overall energy consumption, both data centres have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for existing data centres, achieving optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) 13. In 2023, the HKMA's two data centres were awarded "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings respectively under the "BEAM Plus Existing Data Centres" assessment guidelines issued in 2021; the HKMA is the first and only organisation in Hong Kong to receive such ratings. Enhancing the energy efficiency of the two data centres has always been a key focus of the technical team. To this end, the team adopted green designs in fitting-out works and employed energy-efficient good practices to lower the PUE and achieve relevant targets, including 24-hour monitoring of the environmental facilities in the data centres and continuous enhancement of environmental factors such as air flow and temperature settings. As the technical team continuously improves energy use in the data centres, the HKMA engaged an external consultant in December 2021 to conduct a review to comprehensively assess the green level of the data centres and formulate recommendations to further enhance performance in all aspects. The study was completed in mid-2022. Shortly after the completion of the study, the HKMA also began preparing to obtain the "Green Data Centre" certification under the "BEAM Plus" certification scheme. The certification process is highly comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the technical team rolled out enhancement measures based on the recommendations of the consultant's report to improve energy performance as well as the health elements of the working environment within the data centres.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) conducted an independent verification of the 2023 environmental data (the "2023 Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The 2023 Data includes the total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, greenhouse gas emissions from business air travel, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste) in 2023, their respective intensities, and the changes in their data compared to the 2015 levels. In addition, the 2023 Data also includes the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the change compared to the level when the HKMA launched the food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emission data is compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (the "GHG Protocol") jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, and also covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison (excluding food waste). The verification scope covers a total of 5 office and warehouse assets, of which 4 offices are located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, and 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and the warehouse is at 5) Roxy Industrial Centre, located in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the verification scope, HKQAA examined representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 5 assets. This verification work was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing the selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checking, and conducted reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and selecting representative data and information for checking. Relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the data. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The HKQAA verification team was not involved in the preparation process of the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance on the 2023 Data and concludes that: the 2023 Data is materially accurate and reliable; the HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Sham Siu Yan, Lead Auditor, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, April 2024

The threat posed by climate change is imminent, making it imperative to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization has confirmed 2024 as the hottest year on record, and the first year in which global temperatures exceeded the critical 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Meanwhile, although global greenhouse gas emissions moderated slightly during the COVID-19 pandemic, they have recently hit new highs, highlighting the inadequacy of current climate change mitigation measures. In the process of tackling global warming, the manifestation of climate-related risks is bound to intensify, with unpredictable impacts on the economy and financial markets. Furthermore, current geopolitical tensions, the increasing fragmentation of the global economic landscape, the potential exacerbation of energy security issues, and an uncertain economic outlook all pose greater challenges for countries in addressing climate change.  The transition to a low-carbon economy requires massive and sustained financial support. Globally, Asia faces the most severe transition challenges. As pointed out by the World Economic Forum, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth but also the region most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. Therefore, Asia plays a critical role in whether the world can successfully achieve the goal of net-zero emissions. As a leading international financial centre in Asia, Hong Kong must strengthen its leading role and fully leverage the power of finance to support and drive the region's transition. To this end, the HKMA published the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (Action Plan) last year, setting out our vision and roadmap for progressively integrating sustainability into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses on enhancing the financial sector's resilience to climate-related risks on the one hand, and assisting the industry in capturing new related opportunities on the other. At the same time, we lead by example and play a pioneering role. The HKMA's sustainability work encompasses four major areas: supporting the banking sector to reach net zero, investing in a sustainable future, financing net zero, and making sustainability more inclusive.  The banking system plays a pivotal role in the net-zero transition of Hong Kong and Asia, but banks themselves also face numerous risks during the transition process. In the Action Plan, we have set ambitious targets, requiring all banks to strive to achieve net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 and net-zero financed emissions by 2050. Concurrently, we require all banks to enhance their disclosures of climate-related risks and opportunities. While continuing to strengthen banks' climate risk management, we also provide guidance on their transition planning to help them enhance their transition capabilities and better manage related risks. We are also undertaking preparatory work with relevant stakeholders to align local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, with a view to further enhancing the industry's transparency in related activities. In addition, we are enhancing the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance launched in May last year to include more sustainable activities (including transition activities). We hope that by providing clear criteria, we can channel more capital into sustainable and transition-related projects.  Climate change brings significant physical and transition risks that may affect the long-term financial performance and value of the Exchange Fund's investments. At the same time, however, it also presents opportunities for the Exchange Fund to achieve growth and drive positive impact. Our experience proves that investment returns and positive sustainability impacts can go hand in hand without conflict. In view of this, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Investment Portfolio of the Exchange Fund by 2050, and have pledged in the Action Plan to support climate transition in Asia through the Exchange Fund's investments. Currently, sustainable investments account for over 10% of the Investment Portfolio. To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and the International Finance Corporation in November last year to accelerate the low-carbon economic transition in Asia through co-investments. Furthermore, we published the inaugural "HKMA ESG Expectations" document in September last year to further encourage fund managers to exercise active ownership and adopt sound sustainable investment practices.  Financing is particularly crucial for accelerating the region's transition. As an international financial hub and the premier location for arranging international sustainable bond issuances for Asian issuers (including Mainland provincial and municipal governments), Hong Kong plays an important role in channeling capital to accelerate the region's transition. The Action Plan outlines the vision of developing Hong Kong into the go-to sustainable financing platform in the region and the goal of fostering innovation in sustainable finance. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the Government Sustainable Bond Programme to promote green bond innovation (including the issuance of the world's first multi-currency digital bonds in February last year), to expanding the scope of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme to cover transition financing instruments in May last year, and launching the Digital Bond Grant Scheme in November last year, we have been committed to encouraging regional issuers to utilize Hong Kong's financial platform to raise the capital needed for decarbonisation and transition.  Achieving a robust transition requires not only capital and innovation but also the support of an inclusive and accessible sustainability ecosystem. This includes reliable sustainability data, highly transparent information disclosure, and industry professionals equipped with relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, we committed in the Action Plan to support the promotion of high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosures, and to strive to bridge the gap in sustainable finance talent and knowledge in the region. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainability disclosures, particularly by providing accessible and user-friendly climate disclosure templates to promote sustainability reporting among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). We also launched the Professional Level module on "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking in November last year to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. In addition, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held in February last year and other events, we engaged people from all walks of life in sustainability discussions, thereby fostering collaboration and innovation.  Internally at the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring that our operations align with our sustainability vision. We pledged in the Action Plan to achieve net-zero emissions in our own operations by 2030, which is 20 years ahead of our original commitment. Furthermore, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainability disclosure standards in accordance with the roadmap promulgated by the Government. We started adopting electric vehicles in 2024 and have incorporated low carbon emissions as a screening factor in our procurement process. At the same time, we continue to improve operational efficiency through digitalisation, foster a culture of sustainability within the organisation, and motivate staff to actively participate in sustainability initiatives.  Multilateral cooperation has always been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and drastic changes in geopolitics have added uncertainties to global climate action. However, climate change is an indisputable fact and is progressively worsening. In the work of tackling climate change, the current situation does not allow for the slightest complacency. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help mitigate the impact of climate risks on Hong Kong's financial system and bring us opportunities in the process. Stepping into 2025, we will continue to forge ahead, spare no effort in advancing sustainability work, and deepen our relationships with like-minded partners. Despite the severe challenges ahead, we will, as always, remain committed to supporting Hong Kong, Asia, and other regions in building a sustainable future.

Climate change is a major challenge of our generation. As an international financial centre and a sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development in Asia and globally. The HKMA published the Sustainable Finance Action Plan (Action Plan) in October 2024, setting out the HKMA's vision in this area, including our future direction, the timeline for achieving various targets, and how we expect the industry to join hands in driving related work. The HKMA plans to strengthen the resilience of the Hong Kong financial industry and the HKMA itself against climate change risks, and drive the transition of the Asian region to a more sustainable economy by formulating strategic policies, enhancing supervisory engagement, and upgrading internal operations. Through active participation in international and regional discussions, the HKMA also strives to exert its influence and participate in the formulation of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at the regional and global levels.  As a banking supervisor, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the climate resilience of the banking sector and supporting banks in maintaining safety and soundness during their transition to net-zero emissions. Our priorities for 2025 include: - Launching a new round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management practices and conducting the third round of consultation sessions to review banks' implementation of the HKMA's relevant supervisory requirements and further strengthen banks' climate risk management capabilities; - Refining the work of incorporating climate risk stress testing into the HKMA's supervisor-driven stress testing framework; - Continuing to advance the work of integrating climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review process; - Commencing preparatory work for formulating relevant supervisory requirements for the local banking sector to implement the Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks to be issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards); - Completing the development of a new module GS-2 of the Supervisory Policy Manual to provide guidance to banks on transition planning; and - Sharing good practices with the industry on climate risk management and the application of Green Fintech.  In addition to being a banking supervisor, the HKMA also plays the role of a facilitator, committed to promoting the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the transition. We have published the first phase of the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance to provide the industry with a tool to identify green and sustainable economic activities and facilitate relevant financing. The HKMA has commenced work on the second phase of the taxonomy to expand its coverage, including adding transition elements, increasing green economic activities, and incorporating climate change adaptation objectives. Furthermore, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will organise another Green Fintech event in 2025 to promote the adoption of Green Fintech solutions by banks.  Hong Kong is well-positioned to support the sustainable financing needs in the region. To consolidate this role, we will continue to assist the Government in implementing the Government Sustainable Bond Programme, the expanded scope of which will cover sustainable projects, such as social projects. This move will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and serve as a demonstration for other potential issuers in the region. In addition, we will continue to provide subsidies through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme to encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong's financing platform to raise sustainable funds. We will also step up promotional efforts to encourage more governments, institutions, and enterprises from the Mainland and other regions to raise green funds in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including providing subsidies to prospective issuers of digital green bonds through the Digital Bond Grant Scheme.  Despite the growing market demand for high-quality sustainability disclosures by institutions and enterprises, different entities vary in their capabilities and readiness to make sustainability disclosures, and some entities may require additional guidance and support. In view of this, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to make sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their customers with richer climate disclosure-related tools, including easy-to-use sustainability disclosure templates and accompanying tools; explore how to leverage technology to further make existing resources more user-friendly; and collaborate with major local industry organisations to provide the training needed by the industry.  The sustainable finance market is rapidly evolving, requiring an expansion of the local talent pool and the bridging of knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and the region. The HKMA's key initiatives in 2025 include collaborating with the banking industry to develop professional-level training programmes for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Enhanced Competency Framework on Banking, and identifying areas where the industry has further training needs through the upcoming "Future Banking Skills 2026-2030" study. In addition, we plan to collaborate with key stakeholders to step up the promotion of the Government-subsidised Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme and review the scope of application of the scheme.  At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation (IFC) through the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks to launch targeted initiatives in the Asian region, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market insights, offering targeted upskilling and training support, fostering community connections, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to assist banks in developing roadmaps to make green finance a core business.  As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's Investment Portfolio by or before 2050 to support the transition of the overall economy. We will continuously enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund's investments through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approach, focusing primarily on the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that can promote positive climate outcomes.  The HKMA is committed to leading by example in its corporate sustainability efforts. In response to the accelerated timeline for achieving the net-zero commitment announced in the Action Plan, the HKMA will progressively integrate environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessment, and reporting at a pragmatic pace to continue driving corporate sustainability. Specifically, we will conduct a double materiality assessment in 2025 to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring that we focus on material issues. In addition, we will conduct energy audits and leverage technological solutions to assess the material impacts of climate risks on our offices and operations, with a view to enhancing our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the Hong Kong Sustainability Disclosure Roadmap published by the Government and are actively undertaking preparatory work to make disclosures in accordance with the ISSB Standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment and follow energy efficiency and energy-saving principles in selecting data centres for planned upgrade projects. We will also expand digital initiatives to promote sustainable development and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and enhancing the overall digital experience for our staff, banks, and the public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking supervisor, market enabler, responsible investor, and sustainable organization, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across the Asian region. The HKMA has a robust sustainability governance framework in place to lead the formulation of its relevant strategies and policies; oversee the implementation of related measures; and ensure that sustainability factors are integrated into the HKMA's own operations and practices. In its commitment to practicing good corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency for its sustainability-related work. This governance framework ensures the effective integration of sustainability factors into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and features effective mechanisms to monitor and evaluate the progress and effectiveness of its sustainability efforts. The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises:  - The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee (EFAC) and its relevant Sub-Committees, which are responsible for monitoring and advising on the work of the HKMA, including its sustainability efforts; - The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which is responsible for leading the HKMA's overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategies and policies at the management level; - In terms of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO), which is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG-related work within the EFIO; and - For other functional areas, relevant groups and working groups, which are responsible for planning and executing sustainability measures related to banking and market development, as well as the HKMA's own operations.  At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the efforts of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong.  Given the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA's various sustainability initiatives over the years, we established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability efforts across different functional areas of the HKMA.  - Providing guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans for ESG-related matters across four functional areas: banking, green and sustainable finance ecosystem development, Exchange Fund investment, and internal operations; - Overseeing the implementation of ESG-related plans by various functional departments of the HKMA; - Evaluating the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG targets; and - Overseeing external communication strategies.  The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as standing members. In addition, we invite Executive Directors responsible for key functions related to green and sustainability matters to attend the Steering Committee meetings to report on the major deliverables and future plans of their work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's banking departments, Corporate Development and Operations Department, External Department, and the EFIO.  In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA and the SFC co-initiated the establishment of the Steering Group in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts concerning the financial sector's response to climate and environmental risks, with a view to consolidating Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For details of the Steering Group's work, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening the resilience of Hong Kong's financial system against climate risks, while contributing to Hong Kong's climate targets and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impacts of various sustainability and climate-related issues in their daily business operations, and therefore must proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, banks play an important role in the financial system by channeling funds into green and sustainable projects. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places special emphasis on building banks' capacity to address and manage climate risks, and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy.   In October, the HKMA published the Sustainable Finance Action Plan (Action Plan), setting out its vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a regional sustainable finance hub and support sustainable development in Asia and globally. The Action Plan includes eight goals across four areas. To assist the industry in achieving the objectives of the relevant banking policies, we have been undertaking the following initiatives. All banks to strive to achieve net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 and in their financed emissions by 2050. All banks to enhance the transparency of climate-related risks and opportunities.   In December, the HKMA shared good practices on transition planning with the industry and launched an industry consultation on the draft Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) module GS-2 on "Transition Planning". The new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks' capacity to address the net-zero transition and the related risk management. In addition, we are reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with the aim of incorporating the relevant factors proposed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) for the effective management of climate-related financial risks into the assessment process, and encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks (including transition planning) to address climate risks.   The HKMA has been committed to aligning local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) and the BCBS's Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analyzing the latest developments in sustainability disclosures and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA) in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of the ISSB Standards.   Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the Action Plan. In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (Hong Kong Taxonomy) to address industry concerns about greenwashing and help channel capital flows towards green and sustainable activities. The Hong Kong Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors. It aims to align with the Common Ground Taxonomy as well as the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while incorporating relevant elements to suit local circumstances. We have commenced the second phase of work to expand the coverage of the Hong Kong Taxonomy and are consulting a wide range of stakeholders to further facilitate green and sustainable financing.   During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and committed to supporting banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and address climate change. The HKMA also completed all the work under the two-year plan formulated in 2022 to integrate climate risks into the banking supervisory process. To facilitate banks in strengthening their climate risk management capabilities, the HKMA shared with the banking industry the good practices observed from thematic reviews and consultation meetings, which mainly include: - Establishing a robust governance framework with clearly defined responsibilities for the Board and senior management - Ensuring effective oversight of key areas of climate-related risk matters (1) facilitating and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) exercising appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) building a sound climate risk culture within the institution.  In August, the HKMA hosted a Balanced Supervision Roundtable focusing on climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on various climate risk-related topics, including the challenges faced by banks in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning, and finance. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and facilitated the HKMA's work in climate risk supervision and other related areas.   The HKMA launched a round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in SPM module GS-1 on "Climate Risk Management". The thematic reviews covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing.   The HKMA held a second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new batch of banks in implementing SPM module GS-1 on "Climate Risk Management" and to understand the challenges they faced. The consultation meetings also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provided feedback and guidance based on the specific circumstances of the banks to support their climate risk management efforts.   The HKMA completed the second round of the banking sector Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST) in 2024, with the participation of 21 retail banks and the Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups. The results showed that under various scenarios (including the assumption of concurrent climate risks and macroeconomic downturns), the Hong Kong banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience against severe climate-related shocks. Compared to the pilot CRST, participating banks have significantly enhanced their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risks. A report setting out the CRST results and the good practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025.   The HKMA understands that banks face numerous data and methodological challenges in climate risk management, and has therefore been undertaking various initiatives to promote the adoption of technology to address these challenges. To address the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for conducting climate risk assessments, the HKMA launched the Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform in response to user feedback and by incorporating more local data.   In addition, the HKMA collaborated with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the wider financial services industry. During the year, we published an adoption practice guide and two "Regtech Use Case Briefs" (in English), illustrating technology solutions for Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also organized the third edition of "FiNETech", bringing together over 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore green fintech collaboration.   Deeply aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its ongoing surveillance work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analyses of climate-related risks in its various financial stability reports. By actively participating in the Workstream on Scenario Design and Analysis under the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helped further enrich climate scenarios, assisting central banks and supervisors in understanding the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. In November, the NGFS published the fifth vintage of its long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board (FSB), the HKMA participated in analyzing the interplay between the transition planning of financial and non-financial corporates and financial stability, enabling policymakers to examine climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective.   The HKMA published the "Practical Guide on Green Technology Adoption for Banks" (in English), providing financial institutions with best practices on leveraging green technology to facilitate their net-zero transition.   On the research front, the HKMA conducted several applied research projects to explore the impacts of climate change on the financial sector and the broader economy. Research topics included the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in buffering monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial sector in the transition to a low-carbon economy. The findings of these studies not only enhanced our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability, but also provided valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, which are conducive to relevant policy formulation. Locally, these studies helped strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. The research findings were also shared with a wide range of stakeholders through various channels, including international forums and the HKMA Research Memorandums.   The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (HKIMR), the research arm of the Hong Kong Academy of Finance (AoF), published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provided evidence showing that low-emission firms can benefit significantly from carbon pricing, and highlighted its role in improving efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. The study was featured in the HKIMR's *Insights from Monetary Research* and shared with local and international academics and policy researchers.   The HKMA's Liquidity Facilities Framework is a collateralized standby facility that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework.   The HKMA actively participated in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such participation, we helped facilitate international and regional policy dialogues on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and drew insights to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As set out in the HKMA's Sustainable Finance Action Plan (Action Plan), the HKMA is committed to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by driving net-zero financing and promoting more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to building Hong Kong into the preferred sustainable financing platform for regional and global borrowers, supporting technological innovation in the green sector of the financial market, enhancing sustainable disclosures in the industry, expanding the local green talent pool, and addressing the knowledge gap in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. Building Hong Kong into the preferred sustainable financing platform in the region and globally Catalysing sustainable finance innovation Supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosures Filling the talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in the region To demonstrate the Government's commitment to combating climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and livable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds equivalent to approximately US$28 billion to institutional and retail investors. The funds raised have been allocated to over 110 government green projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, and energy efficiency and conservation. We seize every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors, and distribution channels, laying the foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the impact of the programme and further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub, the scope of the programme was expanded to cover sustainable projects and renamed the Government Sustainable Bond Programme (Sustainable Bond Programme). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the Government publishes the Green Bond Report annually, detailing the allocation of proceeds raised from green bonds and their expected environmental benefits. The HKMA assisted the Government in issuing institutional green bonds equivalent to approximately US$3 billion under the Sustainable Bond Programme in July. This triple-currency issuance covered bonds of various tenors denominated in Renminbi (RMB), US dollars, and Euros. These bonds attracted participation from various types of investors and received an overwhelming response, recording an equivalent of over US$15 billion in subscription amounts. Among them, the 20-year and 30-year RMB green bonds were issued by the Government for the first time, representing the longest-tenor RMB bonds issued by the Government to date, providing a new benchmark for the market and further demonstrating the demonstrative effect of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also further enrich the choices of offshore RMB investment products in Hong Kong. In addition, the enthusiastic response from global investors to the green bonds issued by the Government reflects investors' recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. To encourage more regional borrowers to utilize Hong Kong's financing platform to raise funds for sustainable development, the HKMA continues to implement the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme launched in May 2021, providing subsidies to eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The scheme has been well received by the industry. As of the end of 2024, the scheme had granted subsidies to about 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total amount exceeding US$140 billion. The scheme was extended for three years to 2027 in May 2024, and its scope of subsidies was expanded to cover transition bonds and loans. The purpose of extending and expanding the scheme is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries in the region to utilize Hong Kong's transition financing platform for progressive decarbonisation. - Granted subsidies to about 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total amount exceeding US$140 billion (as of the end of 2024) - Extended for three years to 2027, and expanded the scope of subsidies to cover transition financing instruments At the same time, the HKMA actively promotes Hong Kong's sustainable financing platform, and these efforts have yielded ideal results. Among them, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government issued offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong for the fourth time in August, totaling RMB 7 billion, which included RMB 2.7 billion in green bonds, RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds, and RMB 900 million in social bonds. In September, the Guangdong Provincial People's Government issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, totaling RMB 5 billion, which included RMB 1.5 billion in green bonds. In October, the Hainan Provincial People's Government also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, totaling RMB 3 billion, which included RMB 1 billion in blue bonds and RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds. The aforementioned bond issuance activities repeatedly highlight Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating green and sustainable capital flows between the Mainland and the rest of the world. Leveraging these measures, Hong Kong has been able to consolidate its position as the preferred platform for sustainable financing in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, Hong Kong continued to be the largest hub for arranging the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds in the Asian region in 2024. The total amount of relevant bonds arranged through Hong Kong reached US$43.1 billion, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two landmark tokenised green bonds in 2023 and 2024, namely the world's first tokenised government green bond and the world's first multi-currency digital bond, respectively. These issuances demonstrate the Government's support for regional market participants in applying asset digitalisation and innovative technologies in the green and sustainable finance sector. The HKMA also launched the Digital Bond Grant Scheme in November to promote the issuance of digital bonds in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting the innovative development of the local green and sustainable finance market. The working group on sustainability disclosures under the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group) has been making efforts towards the adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) in Hong Kong. In December 2024, the Government published the Hong Kong Sustainability Disclosure Roadmap, providing a clear pathway for large publicly accountable entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to provide support for entities at different stages of readiness to achieve high-quality sustainability disclosures, making sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. It is worth mentioning that we continue to encourage the application of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies (the Questionnaire), launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template to facilitate sustainability reporting by corporates, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024 to facilitate online completion by corporates (see the QR code below). The HKMA is enhancing the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to make it more user-friendly. Specific measures include selecting core questions from the Questionnaire and providing common use cases for the Questionnaire. In addition, we also strive to improve the compatibility of the Questionnaire with other supporting tools on the Steering Group's website. For more information on the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage. Leading by example, the HKMA demonstrates its commitment by making high-quality sustainability disclosures in its Sustainability Report in accordance with the latest global standards. The report contains rich content on the HKMA's climate-related institutional operational risks, as well as its plans and implementation progress towards achieving its climate targets. For details on the sustainability disclosures of our own operations, please refer to the "Sustainable HKMA" chapter. Given the rapidly changing sustainable finance market, to fill the knowledge and talent gaps, the HKMA is strengthening capacity building in the banking sector and promoting knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners in sustainable finance, the HKMA, together with The Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB), launched the Core Level of the module on Green and Sustainable Finance under the Enhanced Competency Framework (ECF) in July 2023. The module aims to assist banking professionals in acquiring knowledge and developing relevant professional competencies in green and sustainable finance in a more effective manner, and covers four major job roles: (1) Green and Sustainable Finance Products and Services; (2) Sustainability/Climate Risk Management; (3) Sustainability Disclosure and Reporting; and (4) Sustainability Strategy, Compliance and Control. In addition, the Professional Level of the module on Green and Sustainable Finance, targeting mid-level and senior banking practitioners responsible for relevant tasks, was also launched in November. To provide necessary training to banking practitioners, the HKIB, as the administrator of the module on Green and Sustainable Finance, launched the Core Level training programmes for the module in May. Following the launch of the Professional Level in November, the HKMA will collaborate with the banking industry in 2025 to develop training programmes for the Professional Level. To understand the further skills and training needs of the banking industry, the HKMA is currently collaborating with the banking industry to conduct a study on "Future Banking Skills 2026-2030", with the target of publishing the findings in 2025. This joint study is a follow-up to the "Future Banking Skills: 2021-2025" paper published in June 2020. The findings of the follow-up study will provide an important reference for the industry, helping it formulate and adjust talent training strategies and measures to support the sustainable development of the banking sector. Through its collaboration with the Steering Group, the HKMA also continues to assist in implementing the Government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme, which subsidises practitioners, graduates, and students to receive training related to sustainable finance. As of December 2024, a total of 85 international and local courses had been registered as eligible training programmes under the scheme, and over 5,700 reimbursement applications had been approved. The Government announced in the 2025-26 Budget that the scheme will be extended to 2028. The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote capacity building and knowledge sharing through regional and international cooperation. As a founding member of the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment (CASI), the HKMA Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-hosted a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, with discussions revolving around global sustainable finance markets, policy frameworks, and innovative instruments. Furthermore, the HKMA supported the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) in establishing a chapter in Hong Kong in October, and will leverage GFANZ's network and expertise to strengthen capacity building efforts in transition planning and transition finance.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can be mutually reinforcing, the HKMA adheres to the principle of responsible investment in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritizes sustainable assets, and requires its external investment managers to exercise active ownership. Investing prudently in accordance with the principle of "Capital Preservation First, Long-Term Growth", the HKMA believes that paying adequate attention to environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate relevant investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments.  As a committed signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is dedicated to advancing its responsible investment efforts. We place special emphasis on sustainability, particularly the pressing issue of climate change, aiming to enhance the resilience of the Exchange Fund and strive for better risk-adjusted long-term returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment tools to channel capital into sustainable investments across different asset classes (Chart 1).  Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to advancing the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA issued the "HKMA ESG Expectations" and made the document publicly available to investment partners through the annual ESG workshop and the HKMA website. We partner with like-minded investors, regulators, and international organizations to jointly develop industry operating standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment in the financial industry and the central banking community. Through these collaborative efforts, we are committed to fostering a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand.  The HKMA published the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan") in October, setting out the goal of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by or before 2050, and mobilizing partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, further consolidating its commitment to investing in a sustainable future.  The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee (EFAC), chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The primary guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to balance the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund while practicing responsible investment.  The Investment Committee (IC) under EFAC, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring ESG and climate-related risks associated with the Exchange Fund's investments. The IC reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors their implementation through regular meeting reports from the Sustainable Investment Group of the EFIO.  As shown in Chart 2, the ESG Committee under the EFIO, chaired by the Chief Strategist, is responsible for coordinating and monitoring various ESG initiatives of the EFIO. Initiatives and work progress discussed at the quarterly meetings of the ESG Committee are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the EFIO.  In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Strategist of the EFIO, meets regularly to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the EFIO, to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG objectives.  The Sustainable Investment Group works closely with different teams of the EFIO on the integration of ESG factors and assists the senior management of the EFIO in managing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across various investments:  - Public market investments – The Credit, Rules and Monitoring Committee, comprising senior management of the EFIO, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to the advice of the Sustainable Investment Group, and monitors the ESG profile of the fixed income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Compliance Division. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Group participates in the selection, appointment, and monitoring process of external investment managers for the equity portfolio from an ESG perspective (for details, please refer to the section "Promoting Active Ownership" under "Risk Management" on page 39). - Private market investments – The IC, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams for each investment proposal.  The HKMA understands that the physical and transition risks, as well as the associated opportunities brought about by climate change, will affect the long-term financial performance of the Exchange Fund's investments. The "Emissions Gap Report 2024" published by the United Nations Environment Programme projects that unless there is a massive global mobilization to rapidly cut greenhouse gas emissions, the global average temperature will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Uncertainties surrounding policy changes, technological developments, and behavioral shifts in response to rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and affecting asset valuations. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also pose additional risks of physical damage and financial loss to investments. Amid these challenges, the shift towards sustainable solutions by governments and industries also creates potentially attractive long-term investment opportunities in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies, and sustainable infrastructure.  The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places special emphasis on climate-related factors when integrating ESG factors. The HKMA has set a target for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by or before 2050, and continues to advance its efforts through an orderly three-pronged approach to achieve this goal (see Chart 3). The HKMA published the "Action Plan" in 2024, which consolidated the Exchange Fund's commitments and efforts related to climate transition (see Chart 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA prefers active engagement over exclusion or divestment from the investable universe.  Investing in a sustainable future The Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by or before 2050 - Actively expand the scope and variety of sustainable investments, particularly climate transition-themed investments in public and private markets - Integrate ESG factors into every investment decision, with a particular focus on climate change and transition prospect considerations - Formulate clear ESG expectations that align with international standards and best practices, and require all external investment managers, investee companies, and counterparties to comply - Commit to reducing the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio by 67% from the 2017 level by or before 2030  Supporting regional transition through investments - Continue to engage with external investment managers to optimize investment opportunities that drive transition - Continue to explore and prioritize high-quality investment opportunities that can facilitate transition in Asia and generate positive global impacts  First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial to achieving the primary investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially impacting investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies that are undergoing transition and possess superior technology and good corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including those in high-emission industries.  Second, tackling climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding relevant investments or divesting does not help solve the carbon emission problem. Instead, by deploying strategic capital and exercising active ownership to support these industries, the HKMA drives their transition to sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby bringing beneficial changes to themselves and the world. The net-zero investment approach has evolved from preferring green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, so as to drive comprehensive decarbonization across the broader economy.  As a global asset owner, the HKMA understands that the long-term resilience of its portfolio relies not only on the portfolio's own adjustments but also on broad-based economic transition. While there is no single perfect solution, the HKMA refined its responsible investment strategy in 2024, adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive transition while supporting the Exchange Fund and global net-zero targets. The strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including the integration of ESG factors into fundamental analysis and stewardship, portfolio decarbonization tilts, and thematic investments targeting various asset classes that align with the pathway toward net-zero emissions. In public markets, this may involve tilting the portfolio towards ESG leaders or climate solution providers, coupled with stewardship to drive corporate transition. In private markets, there may be a greater focus on investments that facilitate transition.  By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continuously identifies investment opportunities that can facilitate climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's portfolio. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio", with financial performance comparable to relevant portfolio benchmarks (Chart 5).  - Public market investments – The HKMA launched an active global equity portfolio focusing on sustainability and climate transition, and expanded the application of customized low-carbon equity indices to two other portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek Green, Social and Sustainability (GSS) bonds that provide competitive returns while funding sustainable projects (for relevant case studies, see the section "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds"). - Private market investments – The HKMA is committed to building a resilient Long-Term Growth Portfolio, capturing investment opportunities that align with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the HKMA also actively identifies and evaluates investment opportunities that can accelerate the energy transition, including through establishing strategic partnerships with multinational organizations (for examples, see the section "Joining Forces to Tackle Climate Challenges in Asia and Globally").  - Passive portfolios benchmarked against ESG indices - Customized decarbonization strategies for passive and active quantitative portfolios not benchmarked against ESG indices - Active portfolios with a governance theme - Active ESG portfolios themed around sustainability and climate transition - Projects with sustainable features, such as renewable energy infrastructure, and green-certified buildings and warehouses - Funds themed around energy transition and decarbonization globally, in Asia, and in the Global South - Green, Social and Sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organization - The Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP) managed by the International Finance Corporation, focusing on sustainable projects in emerging markets - The "MCPP One Planet" program, providing Paris Agreement-aligned climate-related investments in emerging markets  The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a quasi-governmental organization. The proceeds raised from the green bond were allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading aging equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrade projects cover the optimization of monitoring and control systems and water pump performance, aiming to generate positive environmental benefits from wastewater management, waste reduction, and recycling processes. In addition to the continuous treatment of wastewater and sludge, these facilities compost or repurpose dewatered sludge to produce fertilizers, charcoal, cement, and other building materials, achieving a sludge recycling rate of up to 100%. These facilities also utilize the gas generated during the sludge treatment process to power boilers and generate electricity.  The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a multilateral development bank. The bond provides funding for multiple projects, including the rehabilitation of a national canal system. As one of the largest irrigation systems in the country, the canal is designed to divert excess water flow from rivers to arid regions. The primary objective of the project is to rehabilitate the deteriorating canal lining to prevent seepage, conserve water, improve water use efficiency, and reclaim waterlogged areas. Furthermore, the project conducts skills training for local stakeholders to promote the adoption and optimal use of modern irrigation technologies, such as micro-irrigation, and sustainable farming practices.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable organisation. One of the HKMA's key focuses in fulfilling this commitment in 2024 is the plan to advance the target timeline for achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of the original target, aligning with the Sustainable Finance Action Agenda. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is also committed to fostering staff training and well-being, and strives to promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the primary decision-making body for various corporate sustainability initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA's commitment to climate change, the Steering Committee endorsed a new target in October 2024 for the HKMA to achieve net-zero emissions in its corporate operations by 2030 or earlier, as part of the Sustainable Finance Action Agenda (Action Agenda). At the departmental level, the Executive Director (Corporate Development and Operations) provides guidance on the implementation of sustainability initiatives relating to corporate operations, staff well-being, and community engagement, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division acts as the coordinator and central hub for executing, communicating, and reporting on corporate sustainability initiatives. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Team, comprising staff from different operational departments, provide another layer of support; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming and proposing ideas on creating a green working environment, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of staff participation in volunteer activities. In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, its employees, and the community at large, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the "15 Years Plus Caring Organisation" Logo to the HKMA for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA's sustainability strategy continues to adopt a structure comprising three main pillars: environment, staff, and social responsibility. - Focus on decarbonisation and digitalisation in the HKMA's daily operations, with the target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 or earlier - Adopt green procurement requirements in accordance with government guidelines - Promote greener operational practices to the financial industry and the wider community - Build an engaged workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA's strategic objectives - Foster a collaborative, caring, and inclusive working environment that values diversity and strengthens staff sense of belonging - Provide a quality working environment and promote a healthy lifestyle - Cultivate a culture of caring for the community - Incorporate social considerations into procurement processes and supply chain management - Promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy through consumer education campaigns The HKMA is concerned about climate change and leads by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced its plan to advance the target timeline for achieving net-zero emissions in its own corporate operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of its original commitment, as part of the Action Agenda. The HKMA has revised its roadmap towards the net-zero transition, focusing on responsibly managing the environmental impact of its daily operations, with an emphasis on reducing carbon emissions, conserving energy, reducing paper consumption, and recycling waste, while fully leveraging the improvements in the fuel mix for electricity generation by local power companies. Furthermore, the HKMA has established a digitalised working environment to enhance efficiency while reducing its carbon footprint. In addition, recognising the importance of cultivating a sustainability culture, the HKMA encourages staff to actively adopt sustainable practices through ongoing promotional programmes and activities. Under the overarching 2030 net-zero emissions target, the HKMA has been exploring the adoption of carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and procuring low-carbon products wherever possible. In this regard, since 2023, the HKMA has fully offset the carbon emissions from its air travel by purchasing sustainable aviation fuel and participating in carbon offsetting programmes. The HKMA will expand its carbon insetting and offsetting programmes to cover all remaining major carbon emissions. Apart from the aforementioned environmental commitments regarding physical operations, the HKMA continues to drive the market's low-carbon transition, ranging from the rollout of electronic document submission and processing procedures to the promotion of e-payments and the collection of coins for recirculation. The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA's strategies in leading environmental protection, as well as promoting staff well-being and caring for the community. Under the HKMA's overarching corporate risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing the potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. To more effectively assess the potential impact of climate change on its operations, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and reviewed their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring continuous operations, the design of the HKMA's offices incorporates multiple measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fires, and other emergencies. In addition, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans, incorporating comprehensive measures that cover not only its offices but also its communication and computer facilities. The HKMA conducts regular evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to execute contingency measures. The HKMA has also been monitoring its exposure to transition risks by tracking the greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, and energy and paper consumption arising from its operations. The HKMA's latest climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 associated with its corporate operations by 2030 or earlier. These targets were formulated with reference to the methodology of the Science Based Targets initiative. The HKMA adopts the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its corporate emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA's primary greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect greenhouse gas emissions resulting from the consumption of electricity generated by fossil fuels. In the absence of data from individual suppliers, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimate the major Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital goods) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills and staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculation results for 2023 and 2024 are set out in the "Performance Summary" on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and basis of the verification by the agency are set out in the "Verification Statement" appended at the end of this report. The HKMA leads by example, upholding the same climate-related standards that it expects the banks it regulates and the financial system it oversees to comply with. As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this effort in 2025 to achieve comprehensive green mobility. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, during various renovation projects in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and fitting-out materials or traded in old items for new ones to reduce waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews the energy consumption and energy-saving measures of its offices and data centres, and adopted a modularly designed uninterruptible power supply system in its data centre facility upgrade project in 2024 to further optimise the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus-certified data centres. This design allows for flexible capacity expansion, improves operational efficiency at partial loads, and is equipped with advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping to reduce overall energy consumption. The HKMA enhances internal virtual collaboration through a digital workplace, which, coupled with streamlined workflows, effectively reduces paper consumption. In addition, the HKMA extends the lifespan of its mobile and desktop devices with reference to manufacturers' software update cycles, thereby prolonging the safe usage period of the devices. To reduce waste generated in the office, the HKMA adheres to the "4R" principles—refuse, reduce, reuse, and recycle—and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The HKMA has placed recycling bins at various convenient locations in its offices to collect different materials. To boost the recycling rate, the HKMA added recycling bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit nets in 2024. Furthermore, since November 2022, the HKMA has been sending collected food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA participated in the Environmental Protection Department's "Green Event Pledge", committing to adopting measures to reduce waste generated from various events. The HKMA continues to prioritise the procurement of goods that meet the environmental specifications of the Government's "Green Procurement List", particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan their itineraries carefully, such as consolidating multiple trips whenever possible when attending overseas events. At the corporate level, the HKMA has been purchasing sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing its annual carbon emissions from air travel by approximately 10%. In addition, the HKMA participates in a "Gold Standard" certified carbon offsetting programme to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; this programme focuses on renewable energy generation and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged various learning activities for staff, such as seminars and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. From Earth Day on 22 April 2024 throughout May, the HKMA held its inaugural "HKMA Green Month" under the theme "Think Green, Live Green, Work Green". This provided an excellent opportunity to drive the HKMA's commitment and momentum in practicing environmental sustainability in its internal operations. The campaign featured a "Sustainability BINGO Scorecard" to encourage staff to adopt a green lifestyle, a "Save the Earth" quiz, and a Japanese "Kokedama" indoor plant care workshop; it also included sharing the results of waste audits and a presentation on recycling best practices by a community recycling centre operator. To sustain the momentum of the "Green Month", the HKMA launched an approximately six-month recycling campaign in October, highlighting responsible waste disposal and reminding staff that collective small changes in individual habits can significantly enhance the overall corporate recycling performance. A highlight of the campaign was the launch of the "Green Action" video, featuring several senior executives sharing recycling tips. The campaign also rolled out a series of screensavers, strikingly designed posters, intranet articles, and e-reminders to remind staff to take practical actions to reduce waste and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to gauge their awareness of sustainability and collect their views on proposed green office initiatives. The survey results will help formulate future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong's central banking institution, the HKMA sees itself as a key agent of change and is therefore committed to leading the acceleration of the low-carbon transition and driving the financial industry and the wider community to adopt sustainable practices. The HKMA has rolled out multiple initiatives to enhance the efficiency of its external processes. Following the successful launch of the "Common Data Submission Platform" in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform's service scope in 2024 to cover non-bank institutions, such as Stored Value Facility (SVF) licensees, to facilitate their submission of certain regulatory data. The expansion of the platform's service scope aims to further streamline the submission process for reporting institutions, providing a smoother experience for all users while reinforcing the HKMA's commitment to sustainability. Other new initiatives launched in 2024 include the SurveyTool, which allows banks to respond to HKMA surveys with a simplified submission process, and the Smart Information and Document Management System, a central platform providing users with advanced search functions for bank-related documents.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the environmental data ("Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The Data includes the total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), and greenhouse gas emissions from air travel in 2024, as well as their respective intensities. In addition, the Data also includes Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions generated from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), and employee commuting in 2023 and 2024, and their corresponding intensities. The greenhouse gas emission data of the HKMA is compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol ("GHG Protocol") jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers a total of 6 office and warehouse assets, of which 5 offices are located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre, and the warehouse is at 6) Roxy Industrial Centre, located in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the verification scope, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency examined representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 6 assets. This verification work was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing the selected sample data to their sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checking, and conducted reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanism, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the data, and selecting representative data and information for checking. Relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the information. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team was not involved in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the Data and concludes that: - The Data is materially accurate and reliable; - The overall data collection mechanism of the HKMA is adequate. Shum Siu Yan Head of Audit Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2025
